Bump Microsoft.ApplicationInsights to 3.1.2 and add local telemetry export
items.body:
<!--

- Add a link to the issue this Pull Request relates to.

# Pull request

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Schema compatibility is unresolved; this PR is not ready to roll out on the strength of the version marker.**
> The existing core `telemetry version >= 21` query is **NOT a proven compatible cutover**. A supported newer-platform/older-telemetry-extension combination can report core version 21 while still using the old measurement layout. The [schema-ownership review thread](https://github.com/microsoft/testfx/pull/9725#discussion_r3664994275) remains unresolved; neither extension-owned stamping nor a separate format dimension has been selected.
> This description preserves the original proposal below, but does not approve it. Live Visual Studio/Application Insights ingestion remains unverified. Agent merge remains paused under that decision.

## Summary

<!-- Describe the user-visible change, affected product(s), and related issue. -->

Evidence refreshed on 2026-11-02 for head **`bc59642777621f7eba434eac659377cddf733851`**. Older experiments and current validation are deliberately separated.

### What

Bumps `Microsoft.ApplicationInsights` from `2.23.0` to `3.1.2` and adapts our telemetry extension to the 3.x API. Also adds a network-free local telemetry exporter so collected telemetry can be inspected after the migration.

Fixes part of #7465. Local export verifies the local collector/output branch, **not** live ingestion or equivalence to the service's wire representation.

### Why

AppInsights 2.x was pinned because 3.x initially dropped `netstandard2.0` (see [microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet#3091](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/pull/3091)). That restriction is gone: 3.1.2 ships `netstandard2.0`, `net462`, `net8.0`, `net9.0`, and `net10.0`. 3.x is an OpenTelemetry shim backed by Azure Monitor Exporter, which brings a maintained `System.Diagnostics.DiagnosticSource` transitively.

### Changes

The original implementation/proposal is retained:

- **`Directory.Packages.props`**: `Microsoft.ApplicationInsights` `2.23.0` -> `3.1.2`. Removed the explicit `System.Diagnostics.DiagnosticSource` 6.0.0 pin: its purpose was to override AI 2.x's unmaintained transitive 5.0.0. A newer version now flows through `Azure.Monitor.OpenTelemetry.Exporter` -> `Azure.Core`; keeping the pin caused `NU1605`.
- **`AppInsightTelemetryClient`**: 3.x removed the `metrics` parameter from `TrackEvent`. Numeric measurements are folded into event **properties** as invariant-culture strings and sent through the two-argument overload. This retains a single correlated, context-enriched event and avoids the [OpenTelemetry metric-name restriction](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/blob/main/BreakingChanges.md#metric-name-and-namespace-conventions); property keys do not require metric-instrument renaming.
- **Local export**: `LocalFileTelemetryClient`, selected through the existing `ITelemetryClientFactory` seam by `TESTINGPLATFORM_TELEMETRY_LOCALEXPORTPATH`, writes JSON Lines instead of sending events to AppInsights. Documented in `PACKAGE.md`. Its local `metrics` object contains numeric values; it is not the live 3.x string-valued `customDimensions` representation.
- **Core telemetry version**: the branch changes `TelemetryProperties.VersionValue` from `20` to `21`. That edit is present, but its use as a format/cutover signal remains the unresolved proposal described below.

### Maintenance at the actual revision

| Revision | In-scope maintenance |
|---|---|
| `0dadf79f5748f19da2e03f12d5286ad33a670464` | Preserved and committed the main-branch conflict resolutions, including the current API baselines and async-context behavior. |
| `80e985beeca9c214ba1022e0d7b1a6b126bbc008` | Replaced the shared `TelemetryConfiguration.CreateDefault()` result with a fresh configuration per client. SDK 3.x freezes the shared default after the first client is created. |
| `1f5f218550201cff058a5d7500256ed1d8ae8485` | Integrated current main's translations without changing their content. This is the producer revision for the earlier six-case telemetry package smoke below. |
| `bc59642777621f7eba434eac659377cddf733851` | Raised the existing direct `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Abstractions` minimum from 9.0.4 to **10.0.3**, matching the floor introduced by the AI 3.x/Azure.Core hosting dependency. No CI guard, warning suppression, test assertion, scheduling setting, or supported TFM was changed. |

Build [1659483](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/cbb18261-c48f-4abb-8651-8cdcb5474649/_build/results?buildId=1659483) failed in Windows Debug/Release, Linux Release, and app-model packaging on the same `NU1605`; task logs are 66/109/18/59 respectively. Its synthetic merge `95be83c6c16487497b40e3a2bd46f36453ea98cb` has the same tree (`f85746165f422dc4112e71d3287168dacfd82299`) as `1f5f2185`. The direct DI pin selected 9.0.4 while resolved `Hosting.Abstractions` 10.0.3 required DI abstractions >=10.0.3. Missing artifact-directory messages were downstream effects, not separate root causes.

The replacement [build 1659703](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/cbb18261-c48f-4abb-8651-8cdcb5474649/_build/results?buildId=1659703) was still running when last inspected during this refresh. This is not a claim that required CI is green.

## Design and decision record

<!--
For a new feature, link the maintained design/RFC or docs/decisions/<feature-name>.md.
Include research, approaches actually tried and their outcomes, alternatives,
assumptions, and why this direction was chosen. Challenge material decisions,
especially if the request supplied no rationale. For other changes, link existing
rationale or explain briefly why a separate record is not needed.
-->

Existing rationale is in #7465, the original What/Why/Changes above, and the [held schema discussion](https://github.com/microsoft/testfx/pull/9725#discussion_r3664994275). This maintenance/evidence refresh does not add a new product design or retroactively manufacture a versioned design record. The cutover decision and its maintained decision record remain outstanding.

### Dashboard / Kusto query impact: historical proposal, not an approved contract

AI 2.x writes numeric measurements to `customMeasurements`; the adapted 3.x client folds those values into string-valued event properties, intended for `customDimensions`. Queries reading run timings, counts, timeout settings, parallelization workers, etc. must account for the actual exporter format.

The original proposal bumped the **platform-owned** core version to 21 and suggested this query. It is retained only as historical/proposed design; **do not treat it as a safe production cutover**:

```kusto
customEvents
| extend telemetryVersion = toint(customDimensions['telemetry version'])
| extend runStart = iff(telemetryVersion >= 21,
                        todouble(customDimensions['run start']),
                        toreal(customMeasurements['run start']))
```

The platform and telemetry extension are independently resolvable packages. The [existing compatibility fixture](https://github.com/microsoft/testfx/blob/bc59642777621f7eba434eac659377cddf733851/test/IntegrationTests/Microsoft.Testing.Platform.Acceptance.IntegrationTests/TelemetryForwardCompatibilityTests.cs) explicitly supports a newer platform with telemetry extension 2.0.0. That old extension can still serialize measurements in the old layout while receiving the newer core version. This is a code-traced compatibility counterexample, **not** a claimed live-ingestion/Kusto experiment; the load/run compatibility test does not prove a dashboard schema contract.

Two alternatives have been discussed but **neither selected nor implemented here**: extension-owned stamping of the existing marker, or a separate extension-owned format dimension while preserving core-schema semantics. The review hold remains until that consumer contract is decided.

### Open questions for reviewers

The original questions remain, with current evidence distinguished:

- **Live ingestion under VS 2022 / old .NET SDK runtimes**: 3.x has the required `netstandard2.0`/`net462` assets, but delivery now goes through the heavier Azure Monitor/OpenTelemetry/Azure.Core stack. Local export bypasses ingestion. A live test against a test AI resource on those actual hosts remains outstanding; the standalone `net462` checks below are not a Visual Studio run.
- **Dependency surface**: this brings OpenTelemetry and Azure.Core into a shipping package on all applicable TFMs. Is that acceptable? Successful restore/build does not answer the product/deployment decision.
- **Original package-consumer question, retained as history:** "Should we add a local-export acceptance test (an asset that references the Telemetry extension, opts in, sets the export path, and asserts JSON Lines), in this PR or a follow-up?" Six real package-consumer checks have now been executed in a **session-local harness**; they are not newly checked-in CI acceptance tests. The original suggestion that this would cover the live 3.x ingestion path was too broad: local export selects a different client. No new tests or scope expansion were added by this description refresh.

## Demonstration

<!--
Whenever practical, add screenshots or a short GIF/video showing the feature
working, including terminal/report changes. Add captions, reproduction commands,
and source/package provenance; prefer before/after when behavior changed.
Use a readable text transcript or artifact when clearer, and explain unavailable
or inapplicable media. Redact sensitive data. Media is not test execution proof.
For output/layout changes, record the actual rendered surface, viewport/terminal
dimensions, relevant long-content/empty/error states, and interactions inspected.
Check clipping, wrapping, alignment, and reachable controls. Generated HTML/JSON
or a publishing payload alone does not prove the consuming UI; name inaccessible
hosted/IDE surfaces as validation gaps, not completed visual checks.
-->

This is dependency/lifecycle/serialization work, not a new layout. Text observations are more useful than a screenshot of a green console. The real package smoke observed `PACKAGED_CLIENTS=2`; local-export runs executed the named `TelemetryPackageSmoke` test once and parsed exactly two JSONL records (`testhostbuilt` and `consoletesthostexit`); opt-out runs executed the same test and produced no telemetry file. The exit record's identity/session, current version property, and numeric `run start` metric were checked.

This demonstrates local payload collection and opt-out only. No Visual Studio UI, actual AI service ingestion, dashboard rendering/query, or real UWP app activation is claimed.

## Validation and regression proof

<!--
List each exact command with its result, source state, configuration/TFM, process
exit, executed test identities/counts, and log/result artifact links.
For new regression coverage, retain the tests and remove the relevant production
change in an isolated comparison. Include the intended assertion failure without
the change (red) and the passing run with it (green). Build/restore/launch failures,
zero tests, and skips are not red-phase proof.
For behavior-preserving changes, show green-before/green-after. If a new API
cannot compile on the baseline, use a compiling behavior-removal/mutation check
and label it accurately, or explain why regression sensitivity remains unproven.
For package/acceptance changes, repack each compared state and verify the consumer
uses those bits. State what was not run and any remaining evidence gap.
For features/changed consumer boundaries, map requirements to exact automated E2E
cases and affected consuming surfaces. Assert final identities/grouping, counts,
and each result's associated name/outcome, not just text presence or a correct
intermediate object. Credit adequate existing tests; unit tests or one correct
reporter do not prove another consumer. Include rendered checks/gaps in the map.
See .github/skills/feature-delivery/SKILL.md for the full evidence contract.
-->

Toolchain: repository-pinned **SDK `12.0.100-alpha.1.26509.101`**, Debug configuration. Commands below preserve the executed projects, selectors, switches, and results; machine-specific task-owned result/cache prefixes are normalized to `$evidence` (outside the generated consumer project). Raw binlogs/TRX/generated harnesses are retained in the owning session, not falsely presented as public artifact links. The tables, exact failure, package hashes, and public CI/source links here are the reviewer-accessible evidence.

### Testing: original author-reported history

The original description reported telemetry builds for `netstandard2.0`/`net8.0`/`net9.0`, 612 unit tests on `net9.0` and 611 on `net472` including four new local-client/factory tests, and a removed throwaway AI construct/track/flush smoke. These older counts were **not** re-executed or revision-bound by this maintenance and are not current-head proof.

### Current-head maintenance validation: `bc596427`

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Complete `TestFx.slnx` restore | Exit 0; 0 warnings/errors. The formerly failing hosting graph resolves the required DI floor. |
| `MSTestAdapter.UnitTests` build | Exit 0; existing net462/net48/net8/net9/net10/net11/WinUI matrix retained. |
| `MSTestHostingServiceCollectionExtensionsTests` | 24 discovered/executed/passed on `net8.0`, and 24 on `net462`; no failures/skips. Covers scoped/keyed construction, diagnostics, disposal/error paths, and execution-context isolation. |
| Platform hosting + telemetry selection | 32 executed/passed on each of `net8.0` and `net462`; no failures/skips. **112 focused cases total** across the two assemblies/runtimes. |
| Complete desktop build + pack | **Exit 0; 0 warnings/errors**, all package-family validation and classic UWP targets included. No guards suppressed or TFMs removed. |
| Real packaged-hosting acceptance | **22 planned = selected = executed = passed**, 0 failed/skipped; outer process exit 0. Existing execution verifier checked fresh TRX identities/counters. |

The initial Core-engine full-pack attempt correctly rejected classic UWP. The subsequent "desktop MSBuild unavailable" conclusion was a validation-discovery mistake: the probe omitted `-prerelease`. `vswhere -latest -products * -requires Microsoft.Component.MSBuild -prerelease` found installed VS 18 Insiders. The successful binlog records **`MSBuild\Current\Bin\amd64\MSBuild.exe`, version `18.12.2.51402`**. No installation or global PATH/toolchain edit was needed; only a CMD-process-local PowerShell PATH prefix was used.

<details>
<summary>Executed restore/build/pack and focused runtime commands</summary>

The CMD wrapper was `set "PATH=C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0;%PATH%" && ...`; it affected that process only. From the repository root:

```cmd
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng\build.ps1 -restore -projects TestFx.slnx -msbuildEngine dotnet /bl:artifacts\log\Debug\appinsights-di-restore-{}.binlog
call build.cmd -projects test\UnitTests\MSTestAdapter.UnitTests\MSTestAdapter.UnitTests.csproj -msbuildEngine dotnet '/bl:artifacts\log\Debug\appinsights-di-adapter-tests-{}.binlog'
call build.cmd -pack -msbuildEngine vs '/bl:artifacts\log\Debug\appinsights-desktop-full-pack-{}.binlog'
```

Each final command above exited 0. The earlier `-pack -msbuildEngine dotnet` attempt exited 1 on the unchanged desktop-only UWP check; a scoped hosting pack also hit the existing whole-family package guard. Neither failed attempt is counted as a successful complete pack.

```powershell
$env:TESTINGPLATFORM_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT = '1'
$adapterFilter = '/*/*/MSTestHostingServiceCollectionExtensionsTests/*'
& .\.dotnet\dotnet.exe .\artifacts\bin\MSTestAdapter.UnitTests\Debug\net8.0\Microsoft.VisualStudio.TestPlatform.MSTestAdapter.UnitTests.dll --treenode-filter $adapterFilter --report-trx --results-directory "$evidence\ci1659483-hosting-net8"
& .\artifacts\bin\MSTestAdapter.UnitTests\Debug\net462\Microsoft.VisualStudio.TestPlatform.MSTestAdapter.UnitTests.exe --treenode-filter $adapterFilter --report-trx --results-directory "$evidence\ci1659483-hosting-net462"
$platformFilter = 'FullyQualifiedName~MicrosoftExtensionsHostingExtensionsTests|FullyQualifiedName~AppInsightTelemetryClientFactoryTests|FullyQualifiedName~LocalFileTelemetryClientTests'
& .\.dotnet\dotnet.exe .\artifacts\bin\Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests\Debug\net8.0\Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests.dll --filter $platformFilter --report-trx --results-directory "$evidence\ci1659483-platform-hosting-net8"
& .\artifacts\bin\Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests\Debug\net462\Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests.exe --filter $platformFilter --report-trx --results-directory "$evidence\ci1659483-platform-hosting-net462"
```

All four runtime commands exited 0: 24/24/32/32 passed, no skipped cases. Test assertions and scheduling were unchanged. Validation used parent `1f5f2185` plus exactly manifest blob `5cd7ed874131390cb2975bfee8a182ba158d9b25`; published commit `bc596427` contains that same one-file patch.

</details>

### Current-head shipping packages and consumers

The complete desktop pack produced these aligned local shipping packages, all with nuspec repository commit **`bc59642777621f7eba434eac659377cddf733851`**. These are local `-dev` packages, not a published release:

| Package | Version | SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|
| `MSTest.Extensions.Hosting` | `4.6.0-dev` | `12C03D48EA1D96A28B9E800F58F678C0AFCBB3C78DCF33DF12104E17BDEED061` |
| `Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.Hosting` | `1.0.0-dev` | `CECE244D80B0359C592D36906D951EAE5C468332E6B40A94750A42DEF23DE6EF` |
| `MSTest.TestAdapter` | `4.6.0-dev` | `532C88611A0EC9012A8BDCB56D21B1832D7DAAD21E559DA3BA2000D55AE9F4D6` |

`MSTest.Sdk` and `MSTest.SourceGeneration` were also packed as `4.6.0-dev` from the same commit. The actual hosting nuspec declares DI abstractions 10.0.3 in its net462/net8/net9/net10 groups; net11 is framework-pruned, not removed. Adapter/framework package groups include classic UWP and the existing Windows TFMs.

The [existing generated-DI fixture](https://github.com/microsoft/testfx/blob/bc59642777621f7eba434eac659377cddf733851/test/IntegrationTests/Microsoft.Testing.Platform.Acceptance.IntegrationTests/GeneratedMSTestHostingInjectionTests.cs) and [hosting lifecycle fixture](https://github.com/microsoft/testfx/blob/bc59642777621f7eba434eac659377cddf733851/test/IntegrationTests/Microsoft.Testing.Platform.Acceptance.IntegrationTests/MicrosoftExtensionsHostingTests.cs) consume the packed NuGets, not just source references.

| Consumer requirement | Existing executed evidence |
|---|---|
| DI invocation scopes and constructor discovery | `GeneratedEntryPoint_InjectsHostServicesWithInvocationScopes` and `GeneratedEntryPoint_DiscoverOnlySupportsInjectedConstructors`, each on net462/net8/net9/net10: 8 passes. |
| Expected unsupported cross-AppDomain injection diagnostic | `GeneratedEntryPoint_NetFrameworkExplicitAppDomainFailsWithActionableDiagnostic` and `GeneratedEntryPoint_NetFrameworkExplicitAppDomainExecutionFailsWithActionableDiagnostic`: 2 passes. Their children intentionally fail; outer assertions pass. |
| Host lifecycle and caller/controller cancellation | `RunTestingPlatformAsync_ConsumesPackageAndOwnsHostLifecycle`, `RunTestingPlatformAsync_CallerCancellation_CancelsActiveRun`, and `RunTestingPlatformAsync_ApplicationStopping_CancelsControllerAndActiveTestHost`, each on the four TFMs: 12 passes. |

Fresh generated-consumer caches resolved `Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting` 8.0.0 with DI abstractions 10.0.3 on **net462 and net8**, Hosting 9.0.0/DI 10.0.3 on net9, and Hosting/DI 10.0.12 on net10. Six cached runtime nupkgs were SHA-256 matched to current `artifacts\packages\Debug\Shipping`, and **12 actual net462/net8 DLL payloads** were matched to their packed entries. The consumer's actual `project.assets.json`, cache source metadata, package versions, and `bin\Release\<tfm>` outputs were inspected.

<details>
<summary>Executed package-consuming acceptance commands and execution gate</summary>

```powershell
$project = 'test\IntegrationTests\Microsoft.Testing.Platform.Acceptance.IntegrationTests\Microsoft.Testing.Platform.Acceptance.IntegrationTests.csproj'
$filter = 'FullyQualifiedName~GeneratedMSTestHostingInjectionTests|(FullyQualifiedName~MicrosoftExtensionsHostingTests&FullyQualifiedName!~GeneratedMicrosoftExtensionsHostingTests)'
$env:TESTINGPLATFORM_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT = '1'
& .\.dotnet\dotnet.exe test --project $project -c Debug --no-build --no-launch-profile --list-tests text --filter $filter -p:UsingDotNetTest=true -p:TestingPlatformCommandLineArguments= -p:TestRunnerAdditionalArguments= '-bl:artifacts\log\Debug\hosting-acceptance-discovery-{}.binlog'
# Exit 0; the source-planned 22 named/data cases were discovered.
& .\.dotnet\dotnet.exe test --project $project -c Debug --no-build --no-launch-profile --filter $filter -p:UsingDotNetTest=true "-p:ArtifactsTestResultsDir=$evidence\hosting-acceptance-bc596427-verified" --show-test-results all '-bl:artifacts\log\Debug\hosting-acceptance-run-{}.binlog'
# Exit 0; 22 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. Existing reports/coverage remained enabled.
python .github\skills\testfx-acceptance-validation\scripts\verify_execution.py --trx "$evidence\hosting-acceptance-bc596427-verified\Microsoft.Testing.Platform.Acceptance.IntegrationTests_net12.0_x64.trx" --expected-tests "$evidence\hosting-acceptance-expected-bc596427.json" --started-after $started --process-exit-code 0
# Exit 0; planned=selected=executed=passed=22, failed=skipped=0.
```

`$started` was recorded immediately before the final run; the expected JSON was established from source/data expansion and independent discovery, not copied from the passing TRX. `Microsoft_Testing_TestInfrastructure_TempDirectory_Cleanup=0` retained only task-owned generated assets for provenance inspection; no shared cache was cleared. The final invocation uses the repository's results-directory property once, not a duplicate CLI results option.

</details>

### Earlier lifecycle sensitivity proof: exact eight-case selection

This proof is bound to the pre-fix merge **`0dadf79f5748f19da2e03f12d5286ad33a670464`**, tree **`98944d64881d8ede2a34fcb8c3ab3e19ad238b92`**, versus corrected **`1f5f218550201cff058a5d7500256ed1d8ae8485`**. It is not retroactively called a test run on `bc596427`.

The same eight existing methods and assertions ran on both states:

- `AppInsightTelemetryClientFactoryTests.Create_ReturnsNewAppInsightTelemetryClientInstanceEachCall`
- `AppInsightTelemetryClientFactoryTests.Create_WithNullSessionId_PreservesTelemetryContextValues`
- `AppInsightTelemetryClientFactoryTests.AddAppInsightsTelemetryProvider_WithNonTestApplicationBuilder_ThrowsArgumentException`
- `AppInsightTelemetryClientFactoryTests.AddAppInsightsTelemetryProvider_WithNullBuilder_IsRejectedAsInvalidBuilder`
- `LocalFileTelemetryClientTests.TrackEvent_WritesJsonLine_WithEventPropertiesAndMetrics`
- `LocalFileTelemetryClientTests.TrackEvent_AppendsOneLinePerEvent`
- `LocalFileTelemetryClientTests.TrackEvent_EscapesSpecialCharacters`
- `LocalFileTelemetryClientTests.Factory_WithLocalExportPath_CreatesLocalFileClient`

On the old state **7 passed, 1 failed, 0 skipped; exit 2**. The second real SDK client construction in `Create_ReturnsNewAppInsightTelemetryClientInstanceEachCall` threw:

```text
System.InvalidOperationException:
Configuration cannot be modified after it has been built.
Create a new TelemetryConfiguration instance if you need different settings.
```

The corrected state ran **8/8 passed, 0 failed/skipped; exit 0**. This was an executed contract failure during client construction, not a missing package, compiler error, zero-test selection, or weakened assertion. Method-level/32-worker scheduling was unchanged.

```cmd
rem Pre-fix source tree, before the red invocation: exit 0.
call build.cmd -projects test\UnitTests\Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests\Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests.csproj -msbuildEngine dotnet /p:TargetFramework=net8.0 '/bl:artifacts\log\Debug\appinsights-merge-{}.binlog'
rem Corrected 1f5f2185 source, before the paired green invocation: exit 0.
call build.cmd -projects test\UnitTests\Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests\Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests.csproj -msbuildEngine dotnet '/bl:artifacts\log\Debug\appinsights-final-tests-{}.binlog'
```

```powershell

$filter8 = 'FullyQualifiedName~LocalFileTelemetryClientTests|FullyQualifiedName~AppInsightTelemetryClientFactoryTests'
& .\.dotnet\dotnet.exe .\artifacts\bin\Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests\Debug\net8.0\Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests.dll --filter $filter8 --report-trx --results-directory "$evidence\telemetry-merge-net8"

Each state was built with the pinned repository scripts and a unique binlog; the retained red source tree was subsequently verified identical to the committed pre-fix merge. Other focused runs at `1f5f2185` passed 41 telemetry/provider/factory cases on net8 and 38 on net472; these are older scoped results, not the current 112-case total.

### Earlier six-case real telemetry package smoke: `1f5f2185`

The session-local `TelemetryPackageSmoke` consumer used **`Microsoft.Testing.Platform` and `Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.Telemetry` `2.6.0-dev`**, both packed from `1f5f2185`, with `Microsoft.ApplicationInsights` 3.1.2. The package SHA-256 identities were:

- Platform: `8DB425E384FABA8B277137272992ADA9B57A5D7046000D7A391D245EA7806E79`
- Telemetry: `D2A174AF4B983C3C6FB4F550B33334C4E919A55A2DA4B71B962546B3E00B905F`

These are **not** the newer `bc596427` package hashes above. Fresh cache source metadata and cached-package/executed-DLL hashes were checked against those exact packs.

| Target | Harness case | Observed outcome | Exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| net8.0 | `clients` | Two distinct real AppInsights client constructions; no event-ingestion assertion. | 0 |
| net8.0 | `local-export` | `TelemetryPackageSmoke`: 1 passed; exactly 2 parsed telemetry records, matching exit/session identity and numeric timing field. | 0 |
| net8.0 | `opt-out` | Same named test: 1 passed; no telemetry file. | 0 |
| net462 | `clients` | Two distinct real AppInsights client constructions. | 0 |
| net462 | `local-export` | Same named test: 1 passed; exactly 2 parsed telemetry records with the same checks. | 0 |
| net462 | `opt-out` | Same named test: 1 passed; no telemetry file. | 0 |

The harness was adapted from the existing forward-compatibility asset; no checked-in acceptance test was added. It invoked the packaged clients explicitly, and ran the real packaged test host for local-export/opt-out. Local export's version-21 value was checked as the implemented value, **not** as proof that version 21 universally identifies an exporter layout.

```powershell
# At producer 1f5f2185, both commands exited 0 and verified package content/metadata:
# CMD: call build.cmd -pack -projects src\Platform\Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.Telemetry\Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.Telemetry.csproj -msbuildEngine dotnet '/bl:artifacts\log\Debug\appinsights-telemetry-pack-{}.binlog'
# CMD: call build.cmd -pack -projects src\Platform\Microsoft.Testing.Platform\Microsoft.Testing.Platform.csproj -msbuildEngine dotnet '/bl:artifacts\log\Debug\appinsights-platform-pack-{}.binlog'
$env:NUGET_PACKAGES = "$evidence\telemetry-consumer-cache"
& .\.dotnet\dotnet.exe build "$evidence\telemetry-package-consumer\TelemetryPackageSmoke.csproj" -c Debug -t:Rebuild "-bl:$evidence\telemetry-package-consumer\consumer-isolated-cache-{}.binlog" --nologo -v minimal
# Exit 0, 0 warnings/errors.
& "$evidence\telemetry-package-consumer\Validate.ps1" -ResultsPrefix provenance
# Exit 0, all six case identities/results above verified.
```

**Closed provenance mistake, not an unresolved product incompatibility:** initially the task-local NuGet cache was placed in the consumer's non-hidden `packages` subdirectory. SDK `None Include="**/*"` picked up those DLLs; `ResolveAssemblyReference` searched `@(Content);@(None)` as `CandidateAssemblyFiles` before the correct facade hint path, selecting `Microsoft.NETCore.App.Ref 8.0.31\ref\net8.0\System.Runtime.dll` for net462. That produced 19 `MSB3277` warnings and a pre-`Main` `FileLoadException` (exit -532462766).

Moving **only that owned cache outside the project** fixed the mistake. Consumer project SHA-256 stayed `E88A47F65C57DFA14805CF21F2BF39E519C9E9D7B4FB0DDEF78FB14BF8AE7DFE`; source/package bits, assertions, TFMs, and shared settings were unchanged. The rebuilt legacy executable no longer referenced System.Runtime 8; RAR selected the SDK's proper System.Runtime **4.1.2** facade. All six cases then passed. - Live AI ingestion, VS 2022/other actual IDE hosts, dashboard query/rendering, and servicing/release-branch rollout were not validated.

- The six local telemetry checks are session-local evidence, not newly added CI tests. No executed feature-removal/mutation proof is claimed for the original metrics-to-properties feature itself.

items.body:
I was looking into an issue where Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.Telemetry on .net 9 was still fetching System.Diagnostics.DiagnosticSource 5.0.0 due to Microsoft.ApplicationInsights dependency. I noticed that Microsoft.ApplicationInsights has released major version 3 which no longer has System.Diagnostics.DiagnosticSource however it no longer supports netStandard2.0 as part of microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet#3091. 

Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.Telemetry and Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.VSTestBridge will need to choose a route:
1. Drop netStandard2.0 in favor of .NETFramework 4.6.2 or higher
2. See if ApplicationInsights restores NetStandard2.0 (dropped due to difficulty with OpenTelemetry microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet#3130)
3. Forever stay on Microsoft.ApplicationInsights 2.23.0
4. Drop ApplicationInsights support

items.title: Fix firewall access in agentic workflows
items.body:
<!-- 
- Add a brief summary of what this Pull Request is about.
- Add a link to the issue this Pull Request relates to.
-->

Recurring firewall denials prevented agents from fetching Git history and querying NuGet metadata, while build/test hosts repeatedly attempted nonessential telemetry uploads. This change addresses the causes found in 56 recent runs across 20 workflow families without disabling the firewall.

- Allow Git HTTPS where workflows need history or PR branches, and add the missing .NET ecosystem to repository-quality analysis, PR fixes, and Dependabot bundling.
- Set the telemetry opt-out at workflow scope, including shared build/review consumers, instead of adding exceptions for the observed regional Application Insights uploads. Remove the mutation improver's regional telemetry exception.
- Regenerate all 18 affected lock files with unchanged permissions and action pins. Document that raw `TCP_DENIED` entries can misleadingly carry HTTP `200`, and quote the shared setup's `GITHUB_PATH` redirection to satisfy strict shell linting.

### Telemetry policy limitation

The maintained gh-aw v0.89.21 `dotnet` ecosystem includes `dc.services.visualstudio.com`, an Application Insights ingestion endpoint. Adding that ecosystem to the three workflows above newly permits that host as well as SDK/package traffic. We retain the maintained bundle for restore compatibility; `DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1` suppresses cooperating .NET, MTP, and MSTest clients but is not a blanket firewall ban on telemetry. The regional `*.in.applicationinsights.azure.com` exception remains removed. The local replay below proves denial of the specific regional endpoint tested, not every telemetry destination.

## Validation

Passed: all 18 workflows compiled in strict mode with shellcheck, with zero compiler warnings:

```powershell
gh aw compile efficiency-improver code-simplifier perf-improver test-improver adhoc-qa resource-lock-refactoring repository-quality-improver malicious-code-scan pr-fix dependabot-pr-bundler add-tests address-review.agent autofix.agent review.agent review-on-open.agent review-after-autofix.agent msbuild-quality-review mutation-test-improver --strict --shellcheck --no-check-update
```

Passed: repository action-pin audit (2,560 references across 56 files):

```powershell
python .github\scripts\check_action_pins.py
```

Additional local checks passed for each emitted allowlist, inherited telemetry setting, unchanged job permissions, and unchanged action pins. Review follow-up confirmed that all three newly added `dotnet` bundles permit `dc.services.visualstudio.com` but do not permit the regional Application Insights hosts.

A session-only fixture replay using the pinned AWF Squid 0.28.23 image reproduced baseline GitHub/NuGet `TCP_DENIED` decisions, then allowed GitHub, NuGet, and Azure DevOps feed requests (curl exit 0) while still rejecting `southcentralus-0.in.applicationinsights.azure.com` and an unrelated domain (`TCP_DENIED`, curl exit 60). This does not assert that `dc.services.visualstudio.com` is blocked.

Hosted Actions were not redispatched. The local replay verifies the emitted policies using a captured runtime-config fixture, not the complete hosted orchestration.

items.title: [ResourceLock] Declare ResourceLock for real environment-variable mutation in TestHostBuilderTests
items.body:
gh-aw-workflow-id: resource-lock-refactoring

## Selected project and scope

**Project:** `test/UnitTests/Microsoft.Testing.Platform.UnitTests`
**Current parallelization scope:** already opted in — `[assembly: Parallelize(Scope = ExecutionScope.MethodLevel, Workers = 0)]` (`Program.cs`). Every test method is its own scheduling chunk, so intra-class and cross-class conflicts are both live.

## Shared resource

`TestHostBuilderTests.ConnectToTestHostProcessMonitorIfAvailableAsync_MissingPipeName_ReportsPidQualifiedEnvironmentVariable` calls `SystemEnvironment.SetEnvironmentVariable` — the real, process-global `Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable` wrapper, not a mock — to clear and later restore the PID-qualified key `TESTINGPLATFORM_TESTHOSTCONTROLLER_PIPENAME_123456789`. This is category A (process-global state mutation) and was previously undeclared (category C under-declaration): no `[ResourceLock]`/`[DoNotParallelize]` protected it even though the assembly runs `MethodLevel` parallel.

## Resource coverage matrix

| Resource | Direct test writers | Production readers/writers | Tests invoking those paths | Declaration covering it |

Updated [Microsoft.ApplicationInsights](https://github.com/Microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet) from 2.23.0 to 3.1.2.
Release notes _Sourced from [Microsoft.ApplicationInsights's releases](https://github.com/Microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/releases)._ ## 3.1.2 ## Version 3.1.2 - [Fix `HttpException: Request is not available in this context` in the WEB package when calling `TrackDependency` from `Application_Start` in classic ASP.NET. The WEB activity processors now safely handle the case where `HttpContext.Request` is not yet available.](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/pull/3184) - [Fix #​3163: `TelemetryConfiguration.CreateDefault()` on classic ASP.NET now returns a configuration already populated from `ApplicationInsights.config` (connection string, sampling, storage, live metrics, request/dependency tracking, etc.). A new `PreApplicationStartMethod` (`WebApplicationInsightsInitializer`) materializes and populates the singleton before `Application_Start` runs, so customer code calling `TelemetryConfiguration.CreateDefault()` from `Global.asax.cs` no longer gets an empty configuration. The `ApplicationInsightsHttpModule` no longer carries the config-reading bookkeeping. `TelemetryConfiguration.PrependOpenTelemetryBuilderConfiguration` no longer throws if the configuration was already built — it silently skips, so a second `TelemetryClient` constructed against an already-built configuration no longer throws `InvalidOperationException`.](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/pull/3183) ## 3.1.1 ## Version 3.1.1 - Update OpenTelemetry and Azure Monitor dependencies to address known security advisories (e.g. [GHSA-g94r-2vxg-569j](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g94r-2vxg-569j) in `OpenTelemetry.Api` 1.15.1): https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/pull/3174 - OpenTelemetry 1.15.3 - OpenTelemetry.Exporter.Console 1.15.3 - OpenTelemetry.Exporter.InMemory 1.15.3 - OpenTelemetry.Extensions.Hosting 1.15.3 - OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.AspNetCore 1.15.2 - OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.AspNet 1.15.2 - OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.Http 1.15.1 - OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.SqlClient 1.15.2 - Azure.Monitor.OpenTelemetry.Exporter 1.8.0 ## 3.1.0 ## Version 3.1.0 - [Make `TelemetryContext` properties public and propagate them via `TelemetryClient`.](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/pull/3137) - [Add fallback to `APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING` environment variable for Base, Web, and NLog packages when connection string is not set via code.](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/pull/3134) - [Update Azure.Monitor.OpenTelemetry.Exporter to 1.7.0. This includes updated mappings for telemetry context.](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/pull/3154) - [Fix `OTEL_SDK_DISABLED` not being honored when `TelemetryConfiguration.DisableTelemetry` is set in DI scenarios.](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/pull/3156), [#​3157](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/pull/3157) - [Fix `TrackAvailability` ignoring user-specified `Timestamp` on `AvailabilityTelemetry`. The timestamp is now emitted as `microsoft.availability.testTimestamp` so downstream exporters can use the correct event time.](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/pull/3153) - [Added `netstandard2.0` target framework to `Microsoft.ApplicationInsights` package to support customers with shared libraries targeting netstandard2.0.](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/pull/3142) - [Fix `TelemetryClient.Context.Cloud.RoleName` set after construction now applies to all telemetry.](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/pull/3129) - [Fix bug where Debug/Trace level logs from TrackTrace API were not emitted to Application Insights](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/pull/3121) - [Fix Track API calls to not mutate the passed in dictionary if it is readonly](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/pull/3119) - [Fix `NullReferenceException` in `TelemetryClient.Flush()` and `FlushAsync()` when called from DI scenarios](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/pull/3125) - [Fix `ApplicationVersion` ignored: `ApplicationInsightsServiceOptions.ApplicationVersion` is now applied as `service.version` on the OpenTelemetry Resource for both AspNetCore and WorkerService packages](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/pull/3124) - [Fix `HttpRequestExtensions.UnvalidatedGetHeader` always returning empty string instead of the actual header value. Restored max-length enforcement to guard against oversized header values.](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/pull/3126) ## 3.0.0 - [Replaced `netstandard2.0` with `net8.0` target framework in `Microsoft.ApplicationInsights.NLogTarget` package.](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/pull/3102) ## 3.0.0-rc1 - [Removed `netstandard2.0` target framework from `Microsoft.ApplicationInsights`, `Microsoft.ApplicationInsights.AspNetCore`, and `Microsoft.ApplicationInsights.WorkerService` packages.](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/pull/3091) - [The JavaScript in `Microsoft.ApplicationInsights.AspNetCore` has been updated to version 10.](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/pull/3078) - [Centralized package version management](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/pull/3080) - [Update OpenTelemetry dependencies](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/pull/3080), [#​3092](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/pull/3092) - OpenTelemetry 1.15.0 - OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.AspNetCore 1.15.0 - OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.AspNet 1.15.1 - OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.Http 1.15.0 - OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.SqlClient 1.15.0 - [Vendored OpenTelemetry.Resources.Azure resource detectors to NETCORE shared folder, replaced package with vendored implementation](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/pull/3095), [#​3093](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/pull/3093) - [Added support to disable telemetry via TelemetryConfiguration.DisableTelemetry](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/pull/3084) - [Removed `EnabledAdaptiveSampling` and replaced with `TracesPerSecond` and `SamplingRatio`](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/pull/3085) - [Added `EnableTraceBasedLogsSampler` property to `ApplicationInsightsServiceOptions` for ASP.NET Core and WorkerService packages](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/pull/3088) - [Added support for `StorageDirectory` and `DisableOfflineStorage` from `TelemetryConfiguration` in DI scenarios](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/pull/3088) - [Update Azure.Monitor.OpenTelemetry.Exporter dependency to 1.6.0](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-dotnet/pull/3094) ## 3.0.0-beta2 Added - Automatic configuration binding from "ApplicationInsights" section in appsettings.json for both AspNetCore and WorkerService packages with configuration precedence: environment variables > explicit configuration > appsettings.json - Update Azure Monitor Exporter to 1.6.0-beta.2 - Add comprehensive applicationinsights.config support - Add properties in TelemetryConfiguration to configure underlying exporter Bug fix - Fix TrackMetric(MetricTelemetry) unsupported telemetry type error ## 3.0.0-beta1 - The following Application Insights packages in this repo now use OpenTelemetry internally. OpenTelemetry is the industry standard for telemetry collection and provides better interoperability with other observability tools. - Microsoft.ApplicationInsights - Microsoft.ApplicationInsights.AspNetCore - Microsoft.ApplicationInsights.WorkerService - Microsoft.ApplicationInsights.Web - Microsoft.ApplicationInsights.NLogTarget - Classic APIs of the above packages are preserved; calls are translated to OpenTelemetry telemetry. - Other packages not listed above (such as certain auto-collectors and logging adapters that were published from this repo previously) will not have future versions published. >

---

This PR applies a small readability tweak to code merged in the last 24 hours (PR #11452 - single-pass Traits conversion in `TestCaseExtensions.ToUnitTestElementWithUpdatedSource`).

### File Simplified

- `src/Adapter/MSTest.TestAdapter/Extensions/TestCaseExtensions.cs` — split the combined `(traits ??= []).Add(...)` expression into an explicit null-coalescing assignment followed by a separate `Add` call.

### Rationale

The original expression is correct and behaviorally identical, but combining a null-coalescing assignment with an inline method call inside the same statement is slightly harder to scan than two straightforward statements. Per this repository's guidance to prefer explicit, readable code over compact one-liners, the logic is now:

```csharp
traits ??= [];
traits.Add(new TestTrait(trait.Name, trait.Value));
```

instead of:

```csharp

items.title: [ResourceLock] Narrow AzureFoundryChatClientProviderTests scope to EnvironmentVariables
items.body:
gh-aw-workflow-id: resource-lock-refactoring

## Summary

Replaces a class-level `[DoNotParallelize]` with `[ResourceLock(WellKnownResources.EnvironmentVariables)]` on `AzureFoundryChatClientProviderTests` in `test/UnitTests/Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests`.

**Project:** `Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests`
**Current parallelization scope:** `[assembly: Parallelize(Scope = ExecutionScope.MethodLevel, Workers = 0)]` (see `Program.cs`) — the assembly is already parallelized at method level.

**Shared resource / conflicting tests:** All 17 test methods in `AzureFoundryChatClientProviderTests` read and mutate the process-wide `AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT`, `AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT_NAME`, and `AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY` environment variables via `Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable`/`GetEnvironmentVariable` to drive `AzureOpenAIChatClientProvider.IsAvailable`. Each test already snapshots and restores the previous values in `[TestInitialize]`/`[TestCleanup]`, but the raw `Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable` calls are unsafe if two of these tests (or any other test in the assembly that also mutates environment variables) run concurrently, since the state is process-global.

**Why this attribute placement is minimal:** The class previously carried `[DoNotParallelize]`, which serializes it against *every* other test in the assembly regardless of whether they touch the same resource. Replacing it with a class-level `[ResourceLock(WellKnownResources.EnvironmentVariables)]` narrows the effective conflict set to only the other tests in the assembly that declare the same well-known `EnvironmentVariables` resource key (the analyzer-mandated key for `Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable` mutations), while still fully serializing this class against itself and any other environment-variable mutator. This lets the class run in parallel with the large majority of tests in the assembly that never touch environment variables, without weakening the guarantee that made `[DoNotParallelize]` necessary in the first place.

The class-level attribute is safe here because `MSTEST0074` (`UndeclaredProcessGlobalStateMutationAnalyzer`) requires exactly `WellKnownResources.EnvironmentVariables` for any `Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable` call, and every test method (plus `TestInitialize`/`TestCleanup`) in this class performs such mutations, so a class-level lock correctly covers all of them under `MethodLevel` reacquisition semantics (no `ClassInitialize`/`ClassCleanup` state is involved).

## Validation

Workflow run: https://github.com/microsoft/testfx/actions/runs/33946859894

1. `bash ./build.sh` — Build succeeded, 0 errors, 0 warnings (the analyzer initially flagged the raw `Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable` calls with `MSTEST0074` until `[ResourceLock(WellKnownResources.EnvironmentVariables)]` was added).
2. `PATH="$PWD/.dotnet:$PATH" dotnet run --project test/UnitTests/Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests -f net9.0 --no-build -c Debug -- --filter "FullyQualifiedName~AzureFoundryChatClientProviderTests"` — Passed, 20/20 succeeded.
3. `PATH="$PWD/.dotnet:$PATH" dotnet run --project test/UnitTests/Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests -f net9.0 --no-build -c Debug` (full assembly, method-level parallel) — Passed, 1668 succeeded / 37 skipped / 0 failed out of 1705 total.

`DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_SESSIONID=gha-65080725-33946859894-1` was preserved across all commands above.

No assembly-level `Parallelize`/`DoNotParallelize` attribute or other parallelization setting was added, removed, or changed; this project was already parallelized, and this change only narrows an existing class-level exclusion.

items.title: [ResourceLock] Replace [DoNotParallelize] with [ResourceLock] in MSBuildCompatibilityHelperTests
items.body:
Replaces the class-level `[DoNotParallelize]` on `MSBuildCompatibilityHelperTests` (in `test/UnitTests/Microsoft.Testing.Platform.MSBuild.UnitTests`, which already runs with `[assembly: Parallelize(Scope = ExecutionScope.MethodLevel, Workers = 0)]`) with a class-level `[ResourceLock]` on a dedicated custom key.

**Current parallelization scope.** `Microsoft.Testing.Platform.MSBuild.UnitTests` is already opted into `MethodLevel` parallelism via `Program.cs`. The `[DoNotParallelize]` on `MSBuildCompatibilityHelperTests` previously pulled every test in the class out of the parallel set into the sequential tail.

**Shared resource.** `MSBuildCompatibilityHelper`'s three process-wide static caches: `s_msBuildVersion`, `s_supportsMultiline`, `s_supportsTerminalLoggerWithExtendedMessages` (`src/Platform/Microsoft.Testing.Platform.MSBuild/Tasks/MSBuildCompatibilityHelper.cs`).

**Resource coverage matrix:**

| Resource | Direct test writers | Production readers/writers | Tests invoking those production paths | Declaration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `MSBuildCompatibilityHelper` static caches | All 6 tests in `MSBuildCompatibilityHelperTests`: 2 call `SupportsMultiLine()`/`SupportsTerminalLoggerWithExtendedMessages()` directly (lazily populating the caches), 2 use the `WithMSBuildVersion` helper which replaces the backing fields via reflection, 2 call `TryWriteExtendedMessage()` (one via `WithMSBuildVersion`) | `InvokeTestingPlatformTask.HandleRequestAsync` (`src/Platform/Microsoft.Testing.Platform.MSBuild/Tasks/InvokeTestingPlatformTask.Execution.cs`) calls `SupportsMultiLine()`, `SupportsTerminalLoggerWithExtendedMessages()`, and `TryWriteExtendedMessage()` | None — confirmed by grepping the whole repo for `MSBuildCompatibilityHelper` call sites: the only references outside the production file are the 6 tests inside `MSBuildCompatibilityHelperTests.cs` itself. `InvokeTestingPlatformTaskTests.cs` and `MSBuildTests.cs` in the same assembly instantiate other MSBuild tasks (`InvokeTestingPlatformTask` is only ever constructed, never driving `HandleRequestAsync`'s named-pipe request handling; `TestingPlatformEntryPointTask`/`ConfigurationFileTask` are unrelated types) and never reach `MSBuildCompatibilityHelper` | Class-level `[ResourceLock(MSBuildCompatibilityHelperCacheResource)]`, where `MSBuildCompatibilityHelperCacheResource` is a new `private const string` on the test class, per the repo convention of never using a bare string literal key |

Because no other concurrently-runnable test in the assembly reaches `MSBuildCompatibilityHelper`, the class-level lock is both necessary (the 6 tests mutate/read a shared static cache and must not interleave with each other) and sufficient (nothing else in the assembly can observe or race on that cache) — while being strictly narrower than the previous assembly-tail `[DoNotParallelize]` deferral, since the class can now run concurrently with the rest of the assembly instead of being pulled into the sequential phase.

**Why not eliminate the shared state instead?** The caches are internal implementation details of `MSBuildCompatibilityHelper` (a production `internal static class`); rewriting it to avoid static caching is out of scope for this bounded refactoring, and `[ResourceLock]` is the documented fix for exactly this "process-global state that must be coordinated" category per the shared parallel-safety-audit guidance (category A).

**Validation:**
- `bash ./build.sh -projects $(pwd)/test/UnitTests/Microsoft.Testing.Platform.MSBuild.UnitTests/Microsoft.Testing.Platform.MSBuild.UnitTests.csproj` — build succeeded (0 errors).
- `PATH="$PWD/.dotnet:$PATH" dotnet exec artifacts/bin/Microsoft.Testing.Platform.MSBuild.UnitTests/Debug/net9.0/Microsoft.Testing.Platform.MSBuild.UnitTests.dll --filter "FullyQualifiedName~MSBuildCompatibilityHelperTests"` — 10/10 passed, run 3 times in a row to check for new flakiness from the removed `[DoNotParallelize]`, no failures.
- `PATH="$PWD/.dotnet:$PATH" dotnet exec artifacts/bin/Microsoft.Testing.Platform.MSBuild.UnitTests/Debug/net9.0/Microsoft.Testing.Platform.MSBuild.UnitTests.dll` (full assembly, `MethodLevel`/4 workers) — 229 passed, 1 skipped (pre-existing, OS-specific, unrelated to this change), 0 failed.
- Workflow run: https://github.com/microsoft/testfx/actions/runs/37732212973

**Declaration-reconciliation self-review (category C):** the lock's key is private to this test class (not reused elsewhere), so no key-mismatch/near-miss risk; the lock covers every production reader/writer of the resource (not just the one API the changed test calls); the sole observers in the assembly are the 6 tests on this class, all now under the same lock, so there is no concurrent interleaving that can race on the caches with the replacement declaration in place.

No assembly-level `[Parallelize]`/`[DoNotParallelize]`, `MSTestParallelizeScope`/`MSTestParallelizeWorkers`, `.runsettings`, or `testconfig.json` parallelization settings were added or changed — only the class-level attribute on `MSBuildCompatibilityHelperTests`.

>
> The original pull request description is below.

---

## Goal and rationale

`PathContainment.IsUnderDirectory` recomputed `Path.GetFullPath(directory)` + `TrimEnd` + string concatenation, and re-evaluated `RuntimeInformation.IsOSPlatform(OSPlatform.Windows)`, on **every call** — even though the `directory` argument is loop-invariant at both call sites in `RetryOrchestrator.ArtifactRecovery.cs`:
- `CollectRecoveredArtifacts` calls it once per manifest record, up to `RetryArtifactManifest.MaxRecords` (10,000) times per retry-recovery pass, with the same `attemptDirectory` every time.
- `RemoveArtifactsOutsideControllerRoots` calls it inside `allowedRoots.Any(...)` for every artifact, re-normalizing the same 1-2 AppContainer roots each time.

## Focus area

**Code-Level Efficiency** — redundant computation/allocation inside a loop where the inputs are invariant across iterations.

## Approach

- Added `PathContainment.NormalizeDirectoryPrefix(directory)` (the existing prefix-building logic, extracted) and `IsUnderNormalizedDirectory(path, normalizedPrefix)` (the comparison only), plus cached the OS-platform check once as `private static readonly bool IsWindows`.
- `IsUnderDirectory` keeps its original signature/behavior as a convenience wrapper (`NormalizeDirectoryPrefix` + `IsUnderNormalizedDirectory`) for call sites outside a loop (e.g. `RetryArtifactProcessor.SnapshotAttemptArtifacts`, called once per artifact per attempt — left unchanged).
- In `RetryOrchestrator.ArtifactRecovery.cs`, normalize the attempt directory / allowed-roots prefixes **once**, before the per-record / per-artifact loop, and reuse the cached prefix via `IsUnderNormalizedDirectory`.
- Updated `InternalAPI.Unshipped.txt` for the two new internal static members (this project tracks internal API via a separate `InternalAPI/` Roslyn-analyzer pair, distinct from `PublicAPI/`).

## Energy efficiency evidence

**Proxy metric**: execution time (wall clock) + memory allocation, measured via a standalone console benchmark (net8.0 Release, `Stopwatch` + `GC.GetAllocatedBytesForCurrentThread()`, 2,000,000 iterations, simulating the manifest/artifact containment check against a fixed root):

| Version | Time (2M calls) | Allocation/call |
|---|---|---|
| Old (`Path.GetFullPath` + `TrimEnd` + concat + `IsOSPlatform` per call) | 276 ms | 88.0 B |
| New (prefix normalized once, cached `IsWindows`) | 14 ms | 0.0 B |

Isolated the two contributors: `RuntimeInformation.IsOSPlatform` alone is cheap (4 ms/2M, 0 B), so essentially all the win (and 100% of the eliminated allocation) comes from hoisting `Path.GetFullPath`+`TrimEnd`+concat out of the loop — confirming the fix targets the right bottleneck. Lower CPU time and zero incremental allocation per record/artifact directly reduce work done on a real (if bounded, up to 10,000-record) per-run path.

## Green Software Foundation context

- **Energy Proportionality**: makes CPU work scale only with genuinely new input (records/artifacts) rather than re-deriving loop-invariant state on every iteration.
- **SCI**: reduces Energy (E) term for the retry-recovery functional unit with no change to Carbon Intensity or Embodied Carbon.

## Trade-offs

Slightly larger API surface on the internal `PathContainment` helper (two new members) and callers must remember to normalize once and reuse the prefix — documented via an XML-comment-style note on `NormalizeDirectoryPrefix`. No readability regression: the loop bodies actually get slightly clearer (prefix variable named for its purpose).

## Reproducibility

```bash
./build.sh
artifacts/bin/Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests/Debug/net8.0/Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests --filter "PathContainment|ArtifactRecovery|FullyQualifiedName~RetryTests"
dotnet format whitespace TestFx.slnx --verify-no-changes --include src/Platform/Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.Retry/PathContainment.cs src/Platform/Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.Retry/RetryOrchestrator.ArtifactRecovery.cs
```
(The standalone micro-benchmark was a throwaway console app, not committed.)

## Test Status

- `./build.sh` — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests` full suite: **2015/2015 passed** (51 pre-existing skips), incl. `PathContainmentTests` (5/5) and `RetryTests` (74/75, 1 pre-existing skip).
- `dotnet format whitespace --verify-no-changes` — clean on both edited files.

items.title: [test-improver] Add unit tests for TestHostProcessPIDRequestSerializer
items.body:
## Goal `TestHostProcessPIDRequestSerializer` (the `[Embedded]` IPC serializer for the dotnet-test server-mode PID handshake message, wrapping a single `int` field) had zero direct unit test coverage — it was only exercised incidentally through higher-level named-pipe integration paths, never tested for its own serialize/deserialize round-trip or truncated-stream failure handling. ## Approach Swept `src/Platform/Microsoft.Testing.Platform/IPC/Serializers/*.cs` for zero-coverage classes and found this one. Added coverage in `ProtocolTests.cs`, mirroring the existing `TestHostCompletedRequestSerializer` test pattern in the same file: - `TestHostProcessPIDRequestSerializeDeserialize_RoundTripsPID` — round-trips `0`, `1234`, `-1`, `int.MaxValue`, and `int.MinValue` through serialize→deserialize. - `TestHostProcessPIDRequestDeserialize_TruncatedPayloadThrows` — feeding 1/2/3 truncated bytes of the 4-byte int payload throws `TargetInvocationException` wrapping `EndOfStreamException`. `TestHostProcessPIDRequest`/`TestHostProcessPIDRequestSerializer` are `[Embedded]`-linked shared source (not part of the shipped `Microsoft.Testing.Platform.dll` binary reference), so `InternalsVisibleTo` alone isn't sufficient — added `` entries to the test project's existing IPC-serializers `ItemGroup`, matching the neighboring `TestHostCompletedRequest` entries. ## Coverage Impact | Suite | Before | After | |---|---|---| | `Microsoft.Testing.Platform.UnitTests` (net8.0) total tests | 2569 | 2577 | | Failed | 0 | 0 | | Skipped (pre-existing) | 21 | 21 | ## Trade-offs Small, focused addition (2 test methods, 8 cases via `DataRow`) — no new test infrastructure, no maintenance burden beyond the existing serializer-test pattern already used for sibling classes in the same file. ## Reproducibility ``` ./build.sh -restore export PATH="$PWD/.dotnet:$PATH" dotnet build test/UnitTests/Microsoft.Testing.Platform.UnitTests/Microsoft.Testing.Platform.UnitTests.csproj -c Debug -f net8.0 ./artifacts/bin/Microsoft.Testing.Platform.UnitTests/Debug/net8.0/Microsoft.Testing.Platform.UnitTests ``` ## Test Status Build succeeded (0 warnings/errors). items.title: [test-improver] Add unit tests for RetryExtensions.AddRetryProvider
items.body:
## Goal and rationale `RetryExtensions.AddRetryProvider` is the single public wiring entry point for the entire retry-failed-tests feature — it registers the command-line options provider, the test-host application lifetime callback, the composite data-consumer/session-lifetime handler, and the test-host orchestrator. No existing Retry-area test file (`RetryTests`, `RetryDataConsumerTests`, `RetryArgumentsBuilderTests`, `RetryOrchestratorHelperTests`) exercised this method directly — each one constructs its individual extension class in isolation, so a regression that broke the wiring itself (e.g. forgetting to register one piece, or wiring the pieces to different instances) would go undetected. ## Approach Added `RetryExtensionsTests.cs` with 3 tests calling `AddRetryProvider` on a real `ITestApplicationBuilder` and then driving the platform's own build pipeline to verify the registrations: - Command-line options provider discoverable via the internal `CommandLineManager`'s factory list. - Exactly one test-host-orchestrator factory registered, and it builds a `RetryOrchestrator`. - The lifecycle callback, data consumer, and test session lifetime handler all resolve to the **same** `RetryDataConsumer` instance (mirrors the real `TestHostBuilder` pipeline order: lifecycle callback built and registered into the `ServiceProvider` first, then the composite data-consumer/session-lifetime-handler factory is built with a single shared `alreadyBuiltServices` list across both calls). ## Coverage impact | | Before | After | |---|---|---| | `Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests` (net8.0) total | 1876 | 1879 | | Failed | 0 | 0 | ## Trade-offs Uses reflection on the internal `CommandLineManager._commandLineProviderFactory` field to avoid needing to construct a full `IConfiguration` just to call `CommandLineManager.BuildAsync`; this is a bit more coupled to the implementation than an end-to-end call, but keeps the test focused on what `AddRetryProvider` is responsible for. ## Reproducibility ``` export PATH="$PWD/.dotnet:$PATH" dotnet build test/UnitTests/Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests/Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests.csproj -c Debug -f net8.0 ./artifacts/bin/Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests/Debug/net8.0/Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests --filter "FullyQualifiedName~RetryExtensionsTests" ``` ## Test Status Build succeeded (0 warnings/errors) for both net8.0 and net9.0. Targeted suite 3/3 passed. Full `Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests` net8.0 suite: 1879 total, 0 failed, 37 skipped (pre-existing, no regressions). `dotnet format whitespace TestFx.slnx --verify-no-changes --include ` clean (only the expected harmless F#-project warning). --- > [!NOTE] > This was originally intended as a pull request, but the git push operation failed. > > **Original error:** The process '/usr/bin/git' failed with exit code 128 > > **Workflow Run:** [View run details and download bundle artifact](https://github.com/microsoft/testfx/actions/runs/35543089018) > > The bundle file is available in the `agent` artifact in the workflow run linked above.

items.title: [ResourceLock] Replace [DoNotParallelize] with [ResourceLock] for CLITestBase in-process adapter calls
items.body:
gh-aw-workflow-id: resource-lock-refactoring

## Summary

Test project: `test/IntegrationTests/MSTest.Acceptance.IntegrationTests` (MSTest.Acceptance.IntegrationTests.csproj), assembly-parallelized with `[assembly: Parallelize(Scope = ExecutionScope.MethodLevel, Workers = 0)]` (`Program.cs`, unchanged).

Replaces the class-level `[DoNotParallelize]` on three test classes with a shared class-level `[ResourceLock]`, narrowing an over-broad serialization boundary while preserving correctness for the actual shared resource.

## Shared resource

`CLITestBase.DiscoverTests` / `CLITestBase.RunTestsAsync` (`Utilities/CLITestBase.discovery.cs`) drive the MSTest adapter *in-process*: they call `UnitTestDiscoverer.DiscoverTestsInSourceAsync` and `TestExecutionManager.ExecuteTestsAsync`, which mutate the process-wide static `MSTestSettings.CurrentSettings` (via `MSTestSettings.PopulateSettings`), and they also temporarily swap `Environment.CurrentDirectory` around the call. Both are process-global, unbounded state — not something a `TestContext.TestTempDirectory`-style per-test scope can eliminate, since it belongs to the adapter's own execution engine.

These two methods already share a `private static readonly SemaphoreSlim ExecutionLock = new(1, 1)` inside `CLITestBase`, so concurrent callers cannot corrupt each other's in-flight state. What `[DoNotParallelize]` additionally provided is only ensuring no *other* test class calling the same in-process entry points overlaps with these three — the semaphore prevents corruption, not visibility (a test that finishes could still see stale settings mutated by another concurrently-scheduled test using the same shared `MSTestSettings.CurrentSettings`/`CurrentDirectory` if they weren't otherwise serialized at the class level).

## Resource coverage matrix

| Resource | Direct test writers | Production readers/writers | Tests invoking those paths | Declaration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `MSTestSettings.CurrentSettings` (process-wide static) + `Environment.CurrentDirectory` | `CLITestBase.DiscoverTests`, `CLITestBase.RunTestsAsync` (×2 overloads) in `Utilities/CLITestBase.discovery.cs` | `UnitTestDiscoverer.DiscoverTestsInSourceAsync` → `MSTestSettings.PopulateSettings`; `TestExecutionManager.ExecuteTestsAsync` → reads `MSTestSettings.CurrentSettings` throughout (parallelization scope/workers, ordering, timeouts, etc.) | **DiscoveryIdentityTests**: all 7 test methods (`TestsWithoutNamespaceHaveExactAdapterHierarchy`, `ParameterizedTestsHaveUniqueAdapterTestCaseIdsForEveryDataShape`, `TestDataRowsExposeExactMergedCategoriesAndAreFilterable`, `TestDataRowCategoryFilteringWorksOutOfProcess`, `DiscoverInternalsFindsTopLevelNestedGenericAndDynamicDataTests`, `InternalTypeDynamicDataTestRunsOutOfProcess`, `ClsCompliantDataRowsAreDiscoveredAndRun`) call `DiscoverTests()`/`CLITestBase.RunTestsAsync`. **TestCaseFilteringTests**: all 4 test methods (`FilterByFullyQualifiedNameSelectsExactlyTheMatchingTestDuringDiscovery`, `FilterByIdSelectsExactlyTheMatchingTestDuringDiscovery`, `FilterByFullyQualifiedNameSelectsExactlyTheMatchingTestDuringExecution`, `FilterByIdSelectsExactlyTheMatchingTestDuringExecution`) call `DiscoverTests()`/`CLITestBase.RunTestsAsync`. **LegacyLifecycleObjectModelTests**: 3 of its 4 test methods (`LifecycleInheritanceModes_HaveExactPerTestObjectModelMessages`, `InheritedTestMethod_HasDerivedLifecycleAndIsIsolatedFromSiblingResult`, `MultiLevelBeforeEachDerivedClass_HasExactPerTestMessages`) call the private `DiscoverTests(tfm)`/`RunSingleAndAssertAsync` helpers, which forward to `CLITestBase.DiscoverTests`/`CLITestBase.RunTestsAsync`; the 4th method, `LifecycleInheritanceModes_RunInTargetFrameworkHost`, drives a real out-of-process `TestHost` and never touches `CLITestBase`, so it does not need the lock but inherits it harmlessly at the class level. No other class in the assembly calls `CLITestBase.DiscoverTests`/`RunTestsAsync` (verified via `grep -rn "CLITestBase\.(DiscoverTests|RunTestsAsync)"` across the whole project). | New `internal const string CLITestBase.InProcessAdapterExecutionResource` declared as `[ResourceLock]` at the class level on all three classes. |

## Why this placement is minimal and complete

- The key is declared once, as an `internal const` on `CLITestBase` itself (the owner of the resource), and referenced by all three classes — no bare string literals per MSTEST0073/`PreferConstantForResourceLockAnalyzer` convention.
- Class-level placement (not narrower) is required because every real test method in `DiscoveryIdentityTests` and `TestCaseFilteringTests` calls the shared entry points, and 3 of 4 in `LegacyLifecycleObjectModelTests` do; the remaining out-of-process method is unaffected by inheriting the same lock (it simply serializes against a resource it never touches, which is safe, not merely convenient — it does not weaken protection for the other three methods).
- No other class in the assembly calls these entry points, so there is no additional class that would need to declare the same key to close a gap — the resource coverage is exhaustive within the one assembly (`[ResourceLock]` only coordinates intra-assembly; this project runs its own dedicated test host process, so there is no cross-process collision here).
- This is a **narrowing** of an existing `[DoNotParallelize]` (already-parallelized project, category 1 from the workflow instructions) rather than a net-new opt-in: after this change, all three classes can run in parallel with the many other classes in the same assembly that never call `CLITestBase`, while still being fully serialized against each other and any future caller of the same in-process adapter entry points.
- No `[assembly: Parallelize]`/`[assembly: DoNotParallelize]`, `.runsettings`, or `testconfig.json` parallelization setting was touched.

## Validation

Workflow run: https://github.com/microsoft/testfx/actions/runs/34809394603

```
DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_SESSIONID=gha-65080725-34809394603-1 bash ./build.sh -pack
```
Result: **Build succeeded, 0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s)** (Debug, ~5m08s).

```
DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_SESSIONID=gha-65080725-34809394603-1 PATH="$PWD/.dotnet:$PATH" dotnet test \
  test/IntegrationTests/MSTest.Acceptance.IntegrationTests/MSTest.Acceptance.IntegrationTests.csproj \
  -f net11.0 --no-build -c Debug \
  --filter "FullyQualifiedName~DiscoveryIdentityTests|FullyQualifiedName~TestCaseFilteringTests|FullyQualifiedName~LegacyLifecycleObjectModelTests"
```
Result: **Passed — 16/16 tests succeeded** (all 7 `DiscoveryIdentityTests`, all 4 `TestCaseFilteringTests`, all 5 `LegacyLifecycleObjectModelTests` variants including the two out-of-process TFM-parameterized runs).

## Notes

- This project is already parallelized at the assembly level (`[assembly: Parallelize(Scope = ExecutionScope.MethodLevel, Workers = 0)]`), unchanged by this PR — this is a within-scope narrowing, not a new opt-in.

items.title: [ResourceLock] Remove unneeded DoNotParallelize in FfmpegVideoRecorderTests
items.body:
gh-aw-workflow-id: resource-lock-refactoring

## Summary

Removes an over-broad `[DoNotParallelize]` from a single test method in
`test/UnitTests/Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests/FfmpegVideoRecorderTests.cs`.
No `[ResourceLock]` is added — the analysis below shows there is no concurrent
observer of the mutated state, so a lock would add serialization without
any correctness benefit.

## Project and current parallelization scope

`Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests` already opts into MSTest's
`[assembly: Parallelize(Scope = ExecutionScope.MethodLevel, Workers = 0)]`
(`test/UnitTests/Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests/Program.cs`). Every test
method in the assembly is its own scheduler chunk and can run concurrently
with any other method, including across classes. No `.runsettings` or
`testconfig.json` override changes that scope for this project.

## The shared resource and why it is not a race

`ReadSegments_RelativeEntry_CombinesDirectoryAndParsesInvariantNumbers` sets
`CultureInfo.CurrentCulture = CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("fr-FR")` for the
duration of the test, restoring the original value in a `finally` block, and
was previously marked `[DoNotParallelize]` to keep it from racing with other
tests.

Per the parallel-safety-audit taxonomy (category A, culture branch): the
project's target frameworks are `net462`, `net472` (Windows-only, both
>= .NET Framework 4.6), `net8.0`, and `net9.0`
(`test/UnitTests/Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests/Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests.csproj`).
On every one of these targets, `CultureInfo.CurrentCulture` is stored in the
thread's `ExecutionContext` and flows only to that logical test's own
continuations; the .NET thread pool captures and restores `ExecutionContext`
per work item, so the mutated value cannot leak forward into a concurrently
scheduled sibling test. There is no pre-4.6 .NET Framework target in this
project, so the raw-thread-property leak-forward case does not apply.

I confirmed there is no other reachable observer:
- No other test method, `[TestInitialize]`/`[TestCleanup]`, or fixture in
  `FfmpegVideoRecorderTests` or elsewhere in the project reads or writes
  `CultureInfo.CurrentCulture` / `CurrentUICulture`
  (`grep -rn "CurrentCulture\|CurrentUICulture" test/UnitTests/Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests/*.cs`
  shows only read-only `string.Format(CultureInfo.CurrentCulture, ...)` calls
  in unrelated files, all of which are unaffected because they never depend
  on a *particular* culture value, only on `CurrentCulture` being self-consistent
  within their own test).
- The production code under test,
  `FfmpegVideoRecorder.ReadSegments` (`src/Platform/Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.VideoRecorder/FfmpegVideoRecorder.ProcessManagement.cs`),
  parses the segment numbers with `double.TryParse(..., CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, ...)`
  — it never reads `CurrentCulture` at all, so nothing "coverage-gap" reads a
  wider slice of state than the test declares.

Because there is no concurrent reader or writer of the mutated resource, this
is not a latent race under category C's under-declaration rule — the finding
is a category-D over-serialization: a `[DoNotParallelize]` deferring this test
to the sequential tail for no protective reason. The correct fix is
elimination of the unnecessary attribute, not a narrower lock; adding a
`[ResourceLock(WellKnownResources.Console)]`-style key here would only
serialize the test against the phantom conflict without protecting anything
real.

## Attribute placement

The `[DoNotParallelize]` was removed from the single method that carried it.
No other test in the class or project declares `[DoNotParallelize]` or
`[ResourceLock]`, so this change does not touch or interact with any other
declaration in the file.

## Validation

All commands were run with the repo-pinned SDK from `.dotnet/`, correlated via
`DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_SESSIONID=gha-65080725-34440658521-1` (this workflow run).

1. `bash ./build.sh` — build succeeded (0 warnings, 0 errors).
2. Focused run of the edited test, driving the built net9.0 host directly with
   a VSTest-style filter (the project does not register the MTP
   `--treenode-filter`-only bridge for this filter shape):
   ```
   dotnet exec artifacts/bin/Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests/Debug/net9.0/Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests.dll \
     --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ReadSegments_RelativeEntry_CombinesDirectoryAndParsesInvariantNumbers"
   ```
   Result: 1 total, 1 succeeded, 0 failed.
3. Whole `FfmpegVideoRecorderTests` class, 5 consecutive runs under the
   project's real `MethodLevel`/4-worker parallelization, to rule out
   intermittent culture leakage into siblings:
   ```
   dotnet exec artifacts/bin/Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests/Debug/net9.0/Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests.dll \
     --filter "FullyQualifiedName~FfmpegVideoRecorderTests"
   ```
   Result: 7 total / 7 succeeded on every one of the 5 runs.
4. Full assembly run (no filter) to confirm no regression elsewhere in the
   suite under the same parallelization:
   ```
   dotnet exec artifacts/bin/Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests/Debug/net9.0/Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests.dll

items.body:
Follow-up to #10305, which completed the `Directory.*` arm of `SharedFileSystemPathInTestAnalyzer`'s mutating allowlist (`CreateDirectory`, `CreateSymbolicLink`, `Delete`, `Move`, and all six `Set*Time*` members) plus the `[DoNotParallelize]` opt-out branch. That issue deliberately scoped item 2 to `Directory.*`, so the `File.*` arm is still only partially pinned. ### What is covered today `SharedFileSystemPathInTestAnalyzerTests` covers these `File.*` members: `WriteAllText`, `Copy` (both path roles), `Move`, `Replace` (backup role), `Delete`, `OpenWrite` — plus the negative pins for `File.ReadAllText`/`File.Exists`/`File.Open`. ### What is not covered `IsMutatingFileSystemMethod`'s file arm lists many more entries that have no test: - **The exact mirrors of what #10305 just added on the `Directory.*` side**, and therefore the cheapest to add: - `File.CreateSymbolicLink` — same `(path, pathToTarget)` shape as `Directory.CreateSymbolicLink`; the "`pathToTarget` is only read, so a constant target must not be flagged" behavior is unpinned on the `File` side. - `File.SetCreationTime(Utc)`, `File.SetLastAccessTime(Utc)`, `File.SetLastWriteTime(Utc)` — the identical six-member family. The `Directory` equivalent is a `[DataRow]`-driven test that can be mirrored almost verbatim. - **The write/append/create family**, which has a few distinct signature shapes so it does not templatize as cleanly: `WriteAllTextAsync`, `WriteAllBytes(Async)`, `WriteAllLines(Async)`, `AppendAllText(Async)`, `AppendAllLines(Async)`, `AppendText`, `Create`, `CreateText`. - **The attribute/encryption members**: `Encrypt`, `Decrypt`, `SetAttributes`, `SetUnixFileMode`. ### Notes for whoever picks this up - `[ResourceLock]` is **not** an opt-out for MSTEST0077 — the analyzer never calls `HasResourceLockFor`/`HasAnyResourceLock`, unlike `CurrentDirectoryMutation…`/`CultureMutation…`. Do not copy a `WhenResourceLockDeclared_NoDiagnostic` test over from those files. - The `[DoNotParallelize]` opt-out is already covered by #10305 (class-level, method-level, and the fixture-method negative that pins the `IsTestMethod` restriction); there is no need to repeat it per API. - `File.Open` is intentionally excluded from the allowlist and already has a negative test — do not "fix" that. - The analyzer test harness resolves against `ReferenceAssemblies.Net.Net80` on both the `net472` and `net8.0` legs, so .NET 6+ APIs such as `File.CreateSymbolicLink` and `File.SetUnixFileMode` compile fine in the snippets without any `#if` guard. --- Re-verified against current `main` (2026-08-23): all `File.*` allowlist entries listed in this issue are present in `SharedFileSystemPathInTestAnalyzerTests.cs` (`WhenTestMethodCallsMutatingFileMethodWithConstantPath_Diagnostic` DataRow list covers `CreateSymbolicLink`, `SetCreationTime(Utc)`, `SetLastAccessTime(Utc)`, `SetLastWriteTime(Utc)`, `Encrypt`, `Decrypt`, `SetAttributes`, `SetUnixFileMode`, `AppendText`, `CreateText`, `Create`; the write/append/create async family is covered by `WhenTestMethodCallsAsyncMutatingFileMethodWithConstantPath_Diagnostic`; the `CreateSymbolicLink` `pathToTarget`-not-flagged negative case is covered by `WhenTestMethodCreatesFileSymbolicLinkToConstantTarget_NoDiagnostic`). items.title: [perf-improver] Reorder cheap checks before GetFrameworkAssembly in InheritedMemberFromDifferentMSTestVersionAnalyzer
