items.body:
## Goal and Rationale `ToInProgressTestNode` calls `CreateBaseTestNode`, which always calls `AddTestMethodIdentifier`. That method: 1. Calls `ManagedNameParser.ParseManagedMethodName` — a non-trivial string-parsing operation. 2. Allocates a `TestMethodIdentifierProperty` object. However, **every downstream consumer** that processes `TestNode`s immediately early-exits when the node state is `InProgressTestNodeStateProperty`: | Consumer | Code | |---|---| | `TestResultCaptureHelper` | `if (state is null or DiscoveredTestNodeStateProperty or InProgressTestNodeStateProperty)` | | `TrxDataConsumer` | `if (nodeState is null or DiscoveredTestNodeStateProperty or InProgressTestNodeStateProperty)` | | `AzureDevOpsTestResultsPublisher` | `if (state is null or DiscoveredTestNodeStateProperty or InProgressTestNodeStateProperty)` | The `TestMethodIdentifierProperty` is therefore built and then silently discarded on every test-started event. ## Approach Add an `addTestMethodIdentifier` parameter (default `true`) to the private `CreateBaseTestNode` helper. Pass `false` from `ToInProgressTestNode`. ## Performance Evidence **Per test run savings** (10,000-test suite as baseline): - **10,000 fewer** `ParseManagedMethodName` calls (string parsing, index searches, potential `string[]` allocations for parameter types) - **10,000 fewer** `TestMethodIdentifierProperty` object allocations - Reduction in GC pressure proportional to suite size Measurement: this is O(N) in test count and cost-free to verify — removing the call path is the proof. The performance runner Scenario3/Scenario4 pipelines will show reduced allocations under a memory profiler. ## Trade-offs None — the property is provably unused for in-progress nodes. ## Goal and rationale The perf benchmark suite currently has two scenario types: - **Scenario1**: plain tests (100 classes × 100 methods = 10 000 executions) - **Scenario2**: data-driven tests (100 classes × 10 methods × 10 DataRow rows = 10 000 executions) There is no scenario measuring the cost of MSTest's **test lifecycle hooks** (`[TestInitialize]` / `[TestCleanup]`). These methods run for **every test in every class** and their overhead compounds at scale. Understanding this cost is prerequisite to any future optimization of the lifecycle path. ## Approach Added **Scenario3**: 100 test classes × 100 methods = 10 000 executions, where each class has: - A `[TestInitialize]` method (sets a field — minimal body) - A `[TestCleanup]` method (clears the field — minimal body) Both lifecycle methods are `[MethodImpl(NoInlining)]` to prevent JIT from collapsing them. Four pipelines registered (mirroring the existing Scenario2 coverage): | Pipeline name | Parallelism | Runner | |---|---|---| | `Scenario3_Lifecycle_PlainProcess` | MethodLevel | `PlainProcess` | | `Scenario3_Lifecycle_ClassLevel_PlainProcess` | ClassLevel | `PlainProcess` | | `Scenario3_Lifecycle_DotnetTest_PlainProcess` | MethodLevel | `DotnetTestProcess` | The `*PlainProcess*` suffix means these three pipelines are automatically included in nightly runs (`--pipelineNameFilter "*PlainProcess*"`). ## What this enables Comparing Scenario1 vs Scenario3 wall-clock times on the same machine quantifies the per-test cost of: - `TestInitializeMethod` invocation (via `MethodInfo.Invoke` / `GetInvokeResultAsync`) - `TestCleanupMethod` invocation (similar path) - `TestClassInfo.TestInitializeMethodTimeoutMilliseconds` dictionary lookups - Any GC pressure from the additional lifecycle call stack frames ## Trade-offs - 3 additional pipelines increase nightly `*PlainProcess*` run time modestly. items.title: [efficiency-improver] Reduce duplicate filesystem stat calls in TRX reparse-point detection

labels.name: type/automation
labels.description: Created or maintained by an agentic workflow.

items.body:
## Goal and rationale

TRX report merging confines merged attachment paths under a root directory and rejects trees containing a symlink/junction (reparse point) ancestor, to prevent path escapes. The ancestor walk in `HasReparsePointComponent` checked each directory level with `Directory.Exists(current) && IsReparsePoint(current)` — two separate filesystem stat syscalls (`Directory.Exists` then `File.GetAttributes`) per path component. `File.GetAttributes` alone returns everything needed (existence, `Directory` flag, `ReparsePoint` flag) in one call.

## Focus area

**Network & I/O Efficiency** — reducing redundant filesystem syscalls.

## Approach

- Added `DirectoryExistsAndIsReparsePoint(string path)` in `TrxReportEngine.Merge.PathHelpers.cs`: a single `File.GetAttributes()` call wrapped in try/catch (`IOException`/`UnauthorizedAccessException` → `false`, matching `Directory.Exists()`'s silent-false semantics for missing/inaccessible paths), checking both the `Directory` and `ReparsePoint` bits on the one result.
- Updated `HasReparsePointComponent` to call the new helper instead of the double-syscall pattern.
- Updated an equivalent inline `Directory.Exists(mergedInRoot) && IsReparsePoint(mergedInRoot)` check in `TrxReportEngine.Merge.Attachments.cs` to reuse the same helper for consistency and the same savings.
- Kept the existing `IsReparsePoint(string path)` helper untouched — it's still used for **file** (not directory) reparse-point checks elsewhere (`TrxReportEngine.Merge.AttachmentReferences.cs`).
- No change to path-comparison semantics (`PathComparison` remains `Ordinal`); only the reparse-point I/O pattern changed.

## Energy efficiency evidence

**Proxy metric used**: filesystem syscall count per directory component checked (`2 → 1`), since direct wall-clock or energy measurement on this rarely-executed, non-hot-loop path (TRX report merge, run once per merge operation on a handful of ancestor directories) would be dominated by noise rather than reflecting the actual I/O reduction. Halving the syscalls per ancestor level directly reduces kernel transitions and disk/cache lookups, which is the standard proxy for I/O-bound energy cost when the operation is too infrequent to profile meaningfully with wall-clock timers.

**Limitation**: this is a low-frequency code path (attachment merge during TRX report post-processing), so absolute energy savings are small in isolation; the change is offered as a low-risk, always-correct micro-optimisation rather than a hot-path win.

## Green Software Foundation context

- **Hardware Efficiency**: fewer syscalls per operation means less kernel/filesystem-driver work for equivalent functionality — makes better use of the underlying hardware.
- **SCI**: reduces the Energy term of the SCI equation marginally for every merge operation that walks reparse-point ancestors, with no change to functional unit output.

## Trade-offs

- Slightly more code (one new helper) but net a *simpler* call site (single boolean-returning call vs. `&&`-chained double check) — no readability regression.
- Try/catch based exception handling for the "doesn't exist" case is marginally less idiomatic than `Directory.Exists()`, but is a well-established .NET pattern for this exact scenario (single-stat existence+attributes check) and is documented in the added XML doc comment.

## Reproducibility

```bash
./build.sh
.dotnet/dotnet test test/UnitTests/Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.UnitTests -c Debug --filter "FullyQualifiedName~TrxArtifactPostProcessorTests" --no-restore
```

## Test Status

- `./build.sh` — succeeded (0 errors, 0 warnings).
- `TrxArtifactPostProcessorTests` (covers TRX merge/attachment/reparse-point-adjacent behavior) — 16/16 passed (net8.0 + net9.0).

items.body:
## Goal and Rationale `ParsedManagedName.ToProperty()` is called each time a test result is reported through the MTP path — once per test execution for every test method. For the common parameterless case, it always constructs a new `TestMethodIdentifierProperty` with exactly the same immutable values: - All string fields (`namespace`, `typeName`, `methodName`) are `readonly` - `_parameterTypeFullNames` is `[]` (empty, non-mutable) - `assemblyFullName` and `returnTypeFullName` are hardcoded to `string.Empty` Since `ParsedManagedName` is already cached per `TestMethod` via `ConditionalWeakTable` (PR #10366), the same `ParsedManagedName` instance is reused across test executions. Caching the `TestMethodIdentifierProperty` on it for the parameterless case eliminates one heap allocation per test execution for retries, re-runs, and any scenario where the same test runs multiple times in a session. ## Approach - Add `private TestMethodIdentifierProperty? _cachedParameterlessProperty` field to `ParsedManagedName`. - In `ToProperty()`, return `_cachedParameterlessProperty ??= new(...)` when `_parameterTypeFullNames.Length == 0`. - Parameterized tests (non-empty parameters) continue to allocate a fresh property and fresh array copy to prevent aliasing, as before. ## Performance Evidence **Baseline:** Every call to `ToProperty()` allocates a new `TestMethodIdentifierProperty` (2 allocations for parameterized tests: the array copy + the property; 1 for parameterless). **After:** Parameterless tests allocate once (on first call per session) and reuse the cached instance thereafter. **Impact:** Most tests in typical MSTest suites are parameterless. In retry scenarios with `[Retry]` or repeated runs in a session, this saves 1 allocation per test per execution after the first. Example: 1000 tests each retried 3 times → ~3000 allocations saved (~144KB of short-lived objects avoided). ## Trade-offs - **Memory:** Each `ParsedManagedName` gains a nullable reference field (one pointer, 8 bytes on x64). This is negligible given the `ConditionalWeakTable` already holds one `ParsedManagedName` per `TestMethod` for the session duration. - **Complexity:** Minimal — the pattern (`??=` on a nullable backing field) is idiomatic and self-documenting. - **Thread safety:** `ParsedManagedName` is only accessed through `MSTestTestNodeConverter`, which is single-threaded per test session. The `??=` is not thread-safe, but neither is the surrounding code. ## Test Status - `./build.sh -test`: All tests **passed** (0 warnings, 0 errors). - `MSTestAdapter.UnitTests` (contains `MSTestTestNodeConverterTests`) cannot run on Linux CI due to missing .NET Framework 4.8 SDK; expected to pass on CI where net48 is available. ## Reproducibility ```bash ./build.sh -test ``` > [!WARNING] >

items.body:
## Goal and rationale

Add tests for previously untested code paths in `UseOSConditionAttributeInsteadOfRuntimeCheckAnalyzer` (MSTEST0061).

The analyzer has two distinct code paths for extracting the OS platform name from `RuntimeInformation.IsOSPlatform()` calls:
- **Property reference path**: `OSPlatform.Windows`, `OSPlatform.Linux`, etc. — already tested
- **`OSPlatform.Create()` path**: `OSPlatform.Create("Windows")` — not previously tested

Additionally, `OperatingSystem.Is*()` methods for mobile/embedded platforms (iOS, Android, tvOS, etc.) were not tested. These map to platform names that have **no corresponding `OperatingSystems` enum value**, meaning the analyzer fires but the fixer cannot produce a code fix.

## Approach

Four new tests in `UseOSConditionAttributeInsteadOfRuntimeCheckAnalyzerTests`:

| Test | Code Path | Fix? |
|------|-----------|------|
| `WhenOSPlatformCreateWithKnownPlatform_Diagnostic` | `OSPlatform.Create("Windows")` → `TryGetOSPlatformFromIsOSPlatformCall` Create branch | ✅ fixes to `[OSCondition(OperatingSystems.Windows)]` |
| `WhenOSPlatformCreateWithUnknownPlatform_Diagnostic` | `OSPlatform.Create("CustomOS")` → Create branch, no `OperatingSystems` mapping | ❌ analyzer fires, fixer does nothing |
| `WhenOperatingSystemIsIOS_Diagnostic` | `OperatingSystem.IsIOS()` → maps to `"iOS"`, no `OperatingSystems.iOS` | ❌ analyzer fires, fixer does nothing |
| `WhenOperatingSystemIsAndroid_Diagnostic` | `OperatingSystem.IsAndroid()` → maps to `"Android"`, no `OperatingSystems.Android` | ❌ analyzer fires, fixer does nothing |

## Trade-offs

The `WhenOSPlatformCreateWithUnknownPlatform_Diagnostic` and mobile-platform tests confirm that the fixer silently does nothing for unsupported platforms (returns the original document unchanged). This is a known limitation — a future improvement could suppress the code action when no mapping exists.

## Test Status

All 27 tests in `UseOSConditionAttributeInsteadOfRuntimeCheckAnalyzerTests` pass:

items.title: [perf-improver] Cache TestMethodIdentifierProperty per TestMethod to avoid redundant parsing

labels.name: type/automation

items.body:
## Goal and Rationale `MSTestTestNodeConverter.AddTestMethodIdentifier` is called twice per executed test: once when emitting the in-progress node and once when emitting the result node. Each call was independently calling `ManagedNameParser.ParseManagedMethodName` (which scans the method signature and allocates substrings) and constructing a new `TestMethodIdentifierProperty` object — even though the result is purely a function of the immutable `TestMethod.ManagedTypeName` and `TestMethod.ManagedMethodName` strings. ## Approach Cache `TestMethodIdentifierProperty` in a static `ConditionalWeakTable`, keyed on the `TestMethod` instance. - **`ConditionalWeakTable.GetValue` is thread-safe** — the factory may race on first insertion, but only one value is stored; the extra allocation is benign and extremely rare. - **Weak references** allow GC to collect entries as soon as the `TestMethod` is no longer reachable — no unbounded memory growth. - The new `BuildTestMethodIdentifierProperty` private helper separates construction from caching and is invoked only on cache miss. - Field name follows SA1311 (PascalCase for `static readonly`); `[]` collection-expression initializer satisfies IDE0028. ## Performance Evidence Per executed test this removes: | Saved allocation | Notes | |---|---| | 1× `ParseManagedMethodName` call | Scans the full method signature string | | 2× `string` allocations | `namespace` and `typeName` substrings | | 1× `TestMethodIdentifierProperty` allocation | | **Methodology**: code inspection — the `CreateBaseTestNode` call is the common path for `ToDiscoveredTestNode`, `ToInProgressTestNode`, and `ToResultTestNode`. For each executed test `ToInProgressTestNode` and `ToResultTestNode` both call `CreateBaseTestNode → AddTestMethodIdentifier`. The property is provably equal on both calls since `ManagedTypeName` and `ManagedMethodName` are already cached/immutable on `TestMethod`. For test suites with thousands of tests this avoids thousands of redundant parse operations and short-lived heap allocations, reducing GC pressure during test execution. ## Trade-offs - A static `ConditionalWeakTable` is an additional static field. It holds entries until the `TestMethod` objects are GC'd (typically end of test run), which is the intended lifetime. - On first run per `TestMethod` the factory executes identically to the old code — no regression on the first call. - Complexity increase is minimal: one cache lookup replaces direct construction. ## Reproducibility The savings are observable with a memory profiler (e.g. dotMemory, PerfView, or `dotnet-trace`) against a large test suite: ```bash dotnet trace collect --process-id --providers Microsoft-DotNETRuntime:0x1:5 ``` Filter for `MSTestTestNodeConverter` allocations before/after. ## Test Status Build: ✅ `./build.sh` — 0 errors, 0 warnings Tests: ✅ `./build.sh -test` — all unit test suites pass > [!WARNING] >

items.title: [efficiency-improver] Cache compiled Regex instances in Assert.MatchesRegex/DoesNotMatchRegex

labels.name: type/automation
labels.description: Created or maintained by an agentic workflow.

items.body:
## Goal and rationale

`Assert.MatchesRegex(string pattern, ...)` / `Assert.DoesNotMatchRegex(string pattern, ...)` (the string-pattern overloads) constructed a brand-new `Regex` object on every single call via the private `ToRegex` helper — even when called repeatedly with the exact same literal pattern. Regex compilation/parsing is a well-known non-trivial CPU cost, and test suites commonly re-use the same literal patterns across many assertions (e.g. repeated GUID/date/email format checks). Every redundant construction is wasted CPU work with no functional benefit.

## Focus area

**Code-Level Efficiency** — missing caching of a deterministic, pure computation (parsing a regex pattern string into a `Regex` instance is deterministic for a given pattern).

## Approach

Added a `private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<string, Regex> RegexCache` field to `Assert.Matches.cs` and changed `ToRegex(string? pattern)` to use `RegexCache.GetOrAdd(pattern, static p => new Regex(p))` instead of unconditionally allocating `new Regex(pattern)`. This mirrors the existing `ConcurrentDictionary` usage already present elsewhere in the same project (`TelemetryCollector.cs`, `Assert.AreEquivalent.Comparer.cs`), so it introduces no new dependency and matches established code style. The `Regex`-accepting overloads (where the caller already controls the instance/options) are untouched.

## Energy efficiency evidence

**Proxy metric: CPU time (execution time) per call**, since avoiding redundant regex compilation directly reduces CPU cycles spent — the clearest proxy for energy use in this case.

Standalone micro-benchmark (200,000 calls each, after a 1,000-iteration warm-up, Release config, same email-validation pattern used elsewhere in the assertion tests):

| Scenario | Total time | Per-call |
|---|---|---|
| Uncached (`new Regex(pattern)` every call) | ~1023 ms | ~5.12 μs |
| Cached (`ConcurrentDictionary.GetOrAdd`) | ~3 ms | ~0.016 μs |

That's roughly a **300x** reduction in per-call cost once the pattern is cached (only the very first call per unique pattern pays the parsing cost). In a real test suite, most `MatchesRegex`/`DoesNotMatchRegex` calls reuse a small set of literal patterns, so this removes the vast majority of redundant regex construction overhead.

*Limitation*: this is a synthetic micro-benchmark isolating regex construction cost, not a full end-to-end energy measurement. The real-world benefit scales with how often the same literal pattern is reused across a test run.

## Green Software Foundation context

- **Hardware Efficiency**: eliminates repeated, unnecessary CPU work for a deterministic computation, making better use of the CPU cycles already spent.
- **Energy Proportionality**: cost is now proportional to the number of *distinct* patterns used, not the number of assertion calls — a large test suite with many repeated assertions on the same pattern now does much less redundant work.

## Trade-offs

- The cache grows with the number of distinct patterns seen during a test run's lifetime and is never evicted. This is acceptable in practice: test suites typically use a small, fixed set of literal regex patterns, so the cache size is naturally bounded. No unbounded-growth risk expected in typical usage.
- No readability regression — the change is a small, self-contained addition with an explanatory comment.

## Reproducibility

- Build: `./build.sh` (repo root) — succeeded, 0 warnings/errors.
- Tests: built `test/UnitTests/TestFramework.UnitTests` (`.dotnet/dotnet build test/UnitTests/TestFramework.UnitTests -f net9.0 -c Debug`) and ran the resulting binary directly — **1520/1520 tests passed** (0 failed), including existing `MatchesRegex`/`DoesNotMatchRegex` coverage in `AssertTests.MatchesRegex.cs`.
- Micro-benchmark: standalone console app comparing 200,000 iterations of `new Regex(pattern)` vs. `ConcurrentDictionary.GetOrAdd`-cached construction, run in Release configuration after warm-up.

## Test Status

✅ Full repo build succeeded (0 warnings, 0 errors).
✅ `TestFramework.UnitTests`: 1520/1520 passed, 0 failed.

> [!TIP]
> **Your pull request is ready to create! 🎉 ✅**
>
> Everything is OK—the changes have been pushed to branch `efficiency/jsonwriter-static-dispatch-table-634c00ef659ffb9d`. Please review the changes, including any protected files, before creating the pull request.
>
> **[Create the pull request](https://github.com/microsoft/testfx/compare/main...efficiency/jsonwriter-static-dispatch-table-634c00ef659ffb9d?expand=1&title=%5Befficiency-improver%5D%20Make%20Jsonite%20JsonWriter's%20type-dispatch%20table%20static%20(avoid%20per-call%20Dictionary%2Bclosures))**
>
> The original pull request description is below.

---

## Goal and rationale

`Jsonite.JsonWriter` — the JSON serializer used on the net462/netstandard2.0 server-mode code path — rebuilt an 18-entry `Dictionary<Type, Action<object>>`, with 18 closures each capturing the per-call `TextWriter`, inside its constructor **on every single `Serialize()` call**. This code runs on every RPC message and test-node update sent by a server-mode host running on .NET Framework (e.g. classic MSTest test projects talking JSON-RPC to an IDE or `dotnet test`), so the wasted allocation scales with test count.

## Focus area

**Code-Level Efficiency** — redundant per-call allocation of a dispatch table that has no per-instance state and can be built once.

## Approach

Hoisted the dispatch table to a `private static readonly Dictionary<Type, Action<JsonWriter, object>>`, using delegates that take the owning `JsonWriter` as an explicit first parameter (instead of capturing `writer`/`this` in a closure per instance). The instance-scoped `WriteString` calls now go through `w.WriteString(...)`. No behavior change: the table is populated once per process and shared across all `JsonWriter` instances/calls.

## Energy efficiency evidence

**Proxy metrics used**: wall-clock execution time and `GC.GetAllocatedBytesForCurrentThread()` (CPU time and memory allocation are both direct proxies for energy: fewer CPU cycles and less GC/DRAM churn per call).

Benchmarked using the **actual repository source** (`Jsonite/*.cs` copied into a standalone console harness, `!NETCOREAPP` forced so the changed code path runs), serializing a small mix of representative values (`string`, `int`, `double`, `bool`, `Guid`, `DateTime`) 200,000 times:

| | Old (per-call dictionary+closures) | New (static dispatch table) | Improvement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Time | 464 ms | 141 ms | ~3.3x faster |
| Allocated | 740,000 KB (740 MB) | 73,000 KB (73 MB) | ~90% less |

I also verified serialization **output is byte-for-byte identical** before/after for `DateTimeOffset`, an anonymous object, an `int[]` array, a string with escapes, a `long`, and a `float`, using the same standalone harness.

## Green Software Foundation context

- **Energy Proportionality**: the fix removes work that scaled with call count but had zero per-call variability in its result — the dispatch table is process-invariant, so building it once instead of once-per-call makes resource use proportional to actual demand (unique types encountered), not call volume.
- **Hardware Efficiency**: fewer heap allocations mean less GC pressure and better cache locality per call, reducing CPU cycles per RPC message.

## Trade-offs

None of note. Delegates now take an extra `JsonWriter` parameter instead of closing over instance fields, which is a standard pattern for static dispatch tables and does not reduce readability — the intent ("static, allocation-free per-type dispatch") is documented in a comment above the field.

## Reproducibility

```bash
# Build to confirm the netstandard2.0/net462-only code path still compiles:
./build.sh
.dotnet/dotnet build src/Platform/Microsoft.Testing.Platform -c Debug -f netstandard2.0 --no-restore

# Run the .NET-hosted server-mode tests (System.Text.Json path, unaffected but confirms no regression):
.dotnet/dotnet build test/UnitTests/Microsoft.Testing.Platform.UnitTests -c Debug -f net8.0 --no-restore
artifacts/bin/Microsoft.Testing.Platform.UnitTests/Debug/net8.0/Microsoft.Testing.Platform.UnitTests --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ServerMode"
```

The Jsonite-specific test file (`test/UnitTests/Microsoft.Testing.Platform.UnitTests/ServerMode/JsoniteTests.cs`) is `net462`-only and only compiles on Windows CI (`net462` is conditional on `$(OS) == 'Windows_NT'` and this sandbox is Linux), so it could not be run directly here. I validated correctness by copying the actual `Jsonite/*.cs` sources (old vs. new) into a standalone console harness with `!NETCOREAPP` forced, compiling and running both versions, and diffing their output for representative values — all outputs matched exactly.

## Test Status

- `./build.sh` (full repo restore + build, all target frameworks including `netstandard2.0`/`net462`): **0 warnings, 0 errors**.
- `dotnet format whitespace TestFx.slnx --verify-no-changes --include <file>`: clean (after restoring the file's UTF-8 BOM per repo convention).
- `Microsoft.Testing.Platform.UnitTests` (net8.0, full suite): **2564 passed, 0 failed, 21 skipped** (pre-existing skips).
- `Microsoft.Testing.Platform.ServerMode.Client.Sources.UnitTests` (net8.0, full suite): **105 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped** (pre-existing skips).
- `JsoniteTests.cs` (net462-only, Windows-only in CI): not runnable in this Linux sandbox; behavior equivalence independently verified via the standalone harness described above.

items.title: [efficiency-improver] perf: cache bool.Parse results in InvokeTestingPlatformTask

labels.name: type/automation
labels.description: Created or maintained by an agentic workflow.

items.body:
## Goal and Rationale

`InvokeTestingPlatformTask` bridges MSBuild and the test process via a named pipe. During a test run the task streams every line of test-process output through `LogEventsFromTextOutput`. This method was calling `bool.Parse(TestingPlatformCaptureOutput.ItemSpec)` on **every line**, repeatedly parsing the same constant string value for the entire duration of the run.

A similar pattern existed in `HandleRequestAsync`: `bool.Parse(TestingPlatformShowTestsFailure.ItemSpec)` was re-parsed on every `FailedTestInfoRequest`.

Both `ITaskItem` properties are marked `[Required]` and are set once by MSBuild before `Execute()` is called — their values never change during a run. There is no reason to re-parse them.

## Focus Area

**Code-Level Efficiency** — eliminate redundant string-scanning work on the hot output-streaming path.

## Approach

1. Added two private `bool` backing fields (`_captureOutput`, `_showTestsFailure`) to `InvokeTestingPlatformTask`.
2. Initialised them at the very start of `Execute()`, **before** `base.Execute()` is called (which starts the test process and begins producing output). This ensures the values are visible to the background connection-loop task that calls `HandleRequestAsync`.
3. Replaced the `bool.Parse(...)` call-sites with the cached field reads.

## Energy Efficiency Evidence

**Proxy metric**: CPU cycles / instruction count.

`bool.Parse()` must scan the input string character by character, check for case-insensitive equality against `"True"`/`"False"`, and branch. For a test run emitting 10 000 lines of output, this is 10 000 unnecessary string scans. With the cache, each call becomes a single field read — one machine word load.

The change reduces cumulative CPU work proportionally to the number of output lines and failed tests per run. The larger and more verbose the test suite, the larger the saving.

**Green Software Foundation — Hardware Efficiency**: Using the hardware (CPU cache, branch predictor) more efficiently by removing avoidable repeated string parsing. The CPU work reduced here is pure overhead with no functional benefit.

## Trade-offs

No trade-offs. The change makes the code simpler (field read vs. method call) and more correct (explicit intent that these values don't change during execution). Readability is unchanged or improved.

## Reproducibility

The effect can be observed by running a test project under MSBuild and profiling `InvokeTestingPlatformTask.LogEventsFromTextOutput` (e.g., with `dotnet-trace` + `PerfView`). Before the fix, `bool.Parse` will appear as a hot callee; after the fix it is absent.

## Test Status

- `./build.sh` — **succeeded** (0 errors, 0 warnings)
- `Microsoft.Testing.Platform.MSBuild.UnitTests` (net9.0) — **9/9 passed**

However, `System.CommandLine 2.0.0-beta4.22272.1` is a beta from **September 2022** (~4 years old). Sample projects deliberately opt out of CPM, leaving hardcoded versions of WinUI packages silently drifting. The `CtrfPlayground` sample bypasses CPM with an undocumented raw `VersionOverride`. Two prerelease build-tool dependencies lack explanatory comments.

--- ### 🤖 Suggested Improvement Tasks #### Task 1: Upgrade `System.CommandLine` from the 2022 beta **Priority**: High | **Effort**: Small `System.CommandLine 2.0.0-beta4.22272.1` in `Directory.Packages.props` dates from September 2022 and is only used in `test/Performance/MSTest.Performance.Runner/MSTest.Performance.Runner.csproj`. Upgrade to the latest available version or replace with simple `args[]` parsing given that this is internal performance tooling with minimal CLI needs. --- #### Task 2: Sync `Microsoft.WindowsAppSDK` between root CPM and `MSTestRunnerWinUI` sample **Priority**: Medium | **Effort**: Small `Directory.Packages.props` has `Microsoft.WindowsAppSDK 1.8.251003001`, but `samples/public/mstest-runner/MSTestRunnerWinUI/MSTestRunnerWinUI/MSTestRunnerWinUI.csproj` hardcodes `1.8.251106002` (newer patch) and `Microsoft.Windows.SDK.BuildTools 10.0.26100.7175` (not in root CPM at all). Update the root CPM to the versions the sample actually requires and remove the hardcoded versions from the `.csproj`, or add a comment explaining why the sample must override. --- #### Task 3: Add Dependabot entry for `samples/public/` **Priority**: Medium | **Effort**: Small `samples/public/Directory.Packages.props` disables CPM (`ManagePackageVersionsCentrally=false`). items.title: Flush AppInsights telemetry once at end of ingest loop
items.body:
## Summary

Fixes intermittent failures of `MTP_RunTests_SendsTelemetryWithSettingsAndAttributes` on Linux CI.

`AppInsightTelemetryClient.TrackEvent` called `TelemetryClient.Flush()` after every event. ApplicationInsights' `Flush()` synchronously blocks on the network round-trip to `dc.services.visualstudio.com`, which serialized the ingest loop on each event. On slow Linux CI a single blocking flush could exhaust the 3-second `AppInsightsProvider.Dispose` timeout before later queued payloads (notably the MSTest `sessionexit` event) were even read from the channel, so their `Send telemetry event:` trace line never appeared in the diagnostic log.

## Failure evidence

Excerpt from the failing run's diag log:

- `Send telemetry event: dotnet/testingplatform/host/testhostbuilt` at `T+0.23s`
- Test session ends at `T+0.43s`
- `WARNING Telemetry task didn't flush after '3'` at `T+3.43s` (exactly 3s later — the ingest loop was stuck inside a single network flush)
- No `mstest/sessionexit` trace line anywhere — the test asserts on its presence

## Fix

- Remove the per-event `Flush()` from `AppInsightTelemetryClient.TrackEvent`.
- Add `Flush()` to `ITelemetryClient` and implement it as a thin pass-through on the concrete client.
- In `AppInsightsProvider.IngestLoopAsync`, perform a single best-effort `Flush()` in a `finally` block after the channel drains. The call is wrapped in try/catch so telemetry errors never crash the host, and intentionally does not observe `_flushTimeoutOrStop` (cancelling on shutdown would defeat the purpose of the drain).

## Tests

- Existing `AppInsightsProvider` unit tests continue to pass.
- Adds a regression test `Dispose_FlushesTelemetryClientOnceAfterAllTrackedEvents` that verifies:
  1. `Flush` is never invoked while events are still being tracked (no per-event flushing).
  2. After `Dispose`, `Flush` is invoked exactly once and all queued events were tracked in order.

items.title: [Perf Improver] perf: reduce allocations in test discovery and data-driven test execution

labels.name: type/automation
labels.description: Created or maintained by an agentic workflow.

items.body:
🤖 *This PR was created by Perf Improver, an automated AI assistant focused on performance improvements.*

## Goal and Rationale

Eliminate unnecessary heap allocations in two code paths:

1. **`ValidSourceExtensions` (TestSourceHandler)** — The property previously allocated a new `List<string>` on every access. It is called in `AreValidSources()` during test discovery for each source file. Since the list contents are compile-time constants, it can be safely cached as a static readonly field.

2. **`ReflectionTestMethodInfo` (TestMethodRunner)** — `ExecuteTestWithDataSourceAsync` could allocate up to two `ReflectionTestMethodInfo` instances per data row when `testDataSource` is not null and `GetDisplayName` returns null (requiring fallback to `ComputeDefaultDisplayName`). The instance is now created once and reused.

## Approach

- Cache `ValidSourceExtensions` as a `private static readonly` field. All preprocessor branches (`NETFRAMEWORK`, `WINDOWS_UWP`/`WIN_UI`, default) are compile-time-constant, so the collection is always fixed for a given build target.
- Refactor the null-coalescing display name resolution in `ExecuteTestWithDataSourceAsync` to a short-circuit `if/else` block that creates `ReflectionTestMethodInfo` at most once.

## Performance Evidence

**Change 1 — `ValidSourceExtensions`:**
Before: every call to `testSourceHandler.ValidSourceExtensions` allocates a new `List<string>` (2–3 items).
After: zero allocations per call; returns the same cached collection.
Impact: called once per source file in `AreValidSources()` during discovery init.

**Change 2 — `ReflectionTestMethodInfo` in data-driven tests:**
Before: up to 2 `ReflectionTestMethodInfo` allocations per data row when `GetDisplayName` returns null.
After: at most 1 allocation per data row (only when `testDataSource` is not null). Zero allocations when `testDataSource` is null or `displayNameFromTestDataRow` is set.
Impact: proportional to number of data rows in data-driven tests.

## Trade-offs

- The cached `ValidSourceExtensions` collection is an `IEnumerable<string>` backed by an array literal; it is read-only by nature. No risk of mutation.
- The refactored display name logic is semantically equivalent to the original null-coalescing chain; the precedence (`displayNameFromTestDataRow` → `GetDisplayName` → `ComputeDefaultDisplayName` → fallback) is preserved.

## Reproducibility

Build the affected project and run unit tests:
```
export PATH="$PWD/.dotnet:$PATH"
dotnet build src/Adapter/MSTestAdapter.PlatformServices/MSTestAdapter.PlatformServices.csproj -f net8.0
```

For allocation profiling, use dotnet-trace or BenchmarkDotNet with `MemoryDiagnoser` on a data-driven test suite.

## Test Status

`MSTestAdapter.PlatformServices` builds cleanly with 0 warnings and 0 errors on `net8.0`.
The `MSTest.TestAdapter` project has a pre-existing infrastructure build failure (missing `ApplicationInsights` NuGet) unrelated to these changes.

items.title: Separate Test Results and Logs for AssemblyInitialize, AssemblyCleanup, ClassInitialize and ClassCleanup
items.body:
## Summary

Nowadays, MSTest only returns test results and appends the logs to the first executed test case for AssemblyInitialize and ClassInitialize, and appends the logs to the last executed test case for ClassCleanup logs and AssemblyCleanup.
 
## Background and Motivation
Substrate engineers highly depend on test logs and results for debugging failures. When the logs are appended to the first executed or the last one, it makes it difficult for users to debug it or find the logs. We also have test failure analysis based on different types of failures. Especially when there are failures in Initialize, we encourage users to dig more into the failures before checking in. But since there are no AssemblyInitialize/ClassInitialize results, it's impossible for us to provide the failure type. 

## Proposed Feature
MSTest framework to return results as follows:
•    AssemblyInitialize Failed/Succeeded – Output logs
•    ClassInitialize Failed/Succeeded – Output logs
•    TestMethod1 Failed/Succeeded – Output logs
•    TestMethod2 Failed/Succeeded – Output logs
•    ClassCleanup Failed/Succeeded -Output logs
•    AssemblyCleanup Failed/Succeeded -Output logs

items.body:
## Describe the bug

After upgrading to MSTest.TestAdapter >= 3.2.0, we notice that the code coverage report would now include the 'Microsoft.ApplicationInsights' package. 

We run our tests with:
dotnet test --no-build --no-restore --configuration release --logger trx --collect "XPlat Code Coverage" --results-directory TestResults\ /p:ExcludeByAttribute="CompilerGeneratedAttribute"

Here is a sample coverage.cobertura.xml file:
```
<packages>
    <package name="Microsoft.ApplicationInsights" line-rate="0" branch-rate="0" complexity="4821">
      <classes>
        <class name="Microsoft.ApplicationInsights.ActivityExtensions" filename="/_/BASE/src/Microsoft.ApplicationInsights/ActivityExtensions.cs" line-rate="0" branch-rate="0" complexity="7">
          <methods>
            <method name="TryRun" signature="(System.Action)" line-rate="0" branch-rate="0" complexity="4">
              <lines>
                <line number="24" hits="0" branch="True" condition-coverage="0% (0/2)">
                  <conditions>
                    <condition number="5" type="jump" coverage="0%" />
                  </conditions>
                </line>
                <line number="26" hits="0" branch="False" />
                <line number="29" hits="0" branch="True" condition-coverage="0% (0/2)">
                  <conditions>
                    <condition number="22" type="jump" coverage="0%" />
                  </conditions>
                </line>
                <line number="31" hits="0" branch="False" />
                <line number="34" hits="0" branch="False" />
              </lines>
            </method>
```

We do notice that the 'Microsoft.ApplicationInsights' became a new transitive dependency for 'MSTest.TestAdapter', starting from v3.2.0, but we are not sure how come it would affect our test coverage report; and we are not using app insight at all. Is there a way to tell dotnet test to not include the 'Microsoft.ApplicationInsights' package?

## Steps To Reproduce
1) Upgrade MSTest.TestAdapter to >= 3.2.0
2) run tests with dotnet test --no-build --no-restore --configuration release --logger trx --collect "XPlat Code Coverage" --results-directory TestResults\ /p:ExcludeByAttribute="CompilerGeneratedAttribute"
3) check the coverage.cobertura.xml file under the 'TestResults' folder and notice that the 'Microsoft.ApplicationInsights' package is included in the report

## Expected behavior
Report should not include the 'Microsoft.ApplicationInsights' package as it's a transitive dependency from 'MSTest.TestAdapter'
## Actual behavior
Report includes the 'Microsoft.ApplicationInsights' package

items.title: Microsoft.Testing.Platform for xUnit
items.body:
The approach xUnit.net v3 is taking for supporting Microsoft.Testing.Platform (since it already produces executables) is to conditionally use the "create `TestApplication.CreateBuilderAsync` and build it" approach when it understands that it's time to run in that way, vs. letting it run with our entry point.

Our current strategy is to:

- Link all v3 test projects against `Microsoft.Testing.Platform` and `Microsoft.Testing.Platform.MSBuild`
- Set a NuGet package variable via .props file inside the `xunit.v3.core` NuGet package to indicate that a v3 test project is in place
- Ship a (not linked by default) DLL (`xunit.v3.runner.testingplatform`) inside our `xunit.v3.core` NuGet package that has all the `Microsoft.Testing.Platform` logic
- Detect from within `xunit.runner.visualstudio` when it's got a v3 test project, and override the entry point to conditionally dispatch to the code inside `xunit.v3.runner.testingplatform` when it realizes that we're being asked to run inside of `dotnet test`

There are two branches right now that perform this work in concert with one another:

https://github.com/xunit/xunit/tree/microsoft-testing-platform
https://github.com/xunit/visualstudio.xunit/tree/microsoft-testing-platform

My question is about the documentation & support behind the hook. Right now, through a combination of decompilation of `Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.VSTestBridge` (which we are _**not**_ using) and inspecting the logs from `dotnet test` when using that, it appears that `dotnet test` is utilizing a command line option that looks like `--internal-msbuild-node <argument>`.

Based on [this comment](https://github.com/microsoft/testfx/issues/2539#issuecomment-1988009283), this is currently an undocumented and unsupported way to get `dotnet test` to work:

> This is the reason why the option starts with `--internal-`, options that start with it are hidden internal.

So my question is:

When will the interaction between Microsoft.Testing.Platform test frameworks and `dotnet test` become documented and supported? If this isn't the way we should be doing it, then what is the officially supported way to enable `dotnet test` for Microsoft.Testing.Platform test framework implementations that are not based on `Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.VSTestBridge`?
